relation_to_prior_protocols.mover-v3-draft-20260924: The archived full draft. This core carries over its H1 and H3 definitions, restricted as item_set states, and the rules it names. The core governs wherever the two differ.

question: Among US-equity extreme daily movers (population D), does MAX lottery conditioning (H1), or the overnight versus intraday split of the hold (H3), change the sign or size of the cost-net forward return? Continuation is one tested outcome, not the premise.
direction: long only (a short side for the MAX-reversal prior is an open question; borrow, hard-to-borrow fees and SEC Rule 201 were not examined)

item_set.family: m = 5: two primary tests that are not tradable (H1-D, H3-c) and three tradable cells (H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a, H3-b). Holm runs over these five items only.

items.statistic: mean net(b_lane | high MAX21 tercile) - mean net(b_lane | low MAX21 tercile), population D
items.why_kept: The direct test of H1. BCW 2011 predicts that high-MAX names underperform low-MAX names. The high-minus-low difference on one arm is the smallest statistic that tests that prediction. The 5-session b_lane arm is kept because it is the D horizon closest to BCW's holding period.

items.statistic: mean net(b_lane | low MAX21 tercile), population D
items.why_kept: The study is long-only and asks about cost-net returns. The low-MAX tercile is the only H1 cell for which the prior predicts the best relative return, so it is the one cell whose pass would make the conditioning tradable. The high and middle cells (high has a negative prior, middle none) are reported descriptively with no p-value.

The intraday leg as a trade: one regular session, from 09:35 to 15:55 ET on t+1. With H3-b it answers whether either leg is tradable after costs. Neither leg has a sourced direction for movers, so both are kept.
The overnight leg as a trade: from 15:55 ET on t+1 to the first eligible quote from 09:30 ET on t+2. It is the counterpart of H3-a.

items.statistic: mean over events of (mean of the 4 overnight leg log returns - mean of the 4 intraday leg log returns), gross, legs as in arms.c_decomposition
items.alternative: not equal to 0 at every stage; at the holdout a pass also needs the sign of the validation estimate (multiple_testing.no_direction_lock)
items.why_kept: The direct test of H3's 'versus'. It uses official prints only, so it needs no fill and no cost model. The literature (LPS 2019, ABJK 2022) concerns large, liquid names and gives no sign for movers, so the test is two-sided at every stage. It is not locked to the development sign, because development is survivorship-limited (chronology.labels.development) and gates nothing. At the holdout, a confirmatory pass also needs the holdout estimate to have the sign of the governing validation estimate, so a pass replicates the screened direction.

item_set.tradable_cells: H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a and H3-b are tradable cells and nothing else. H1-D and H3-c are primary tests and are never tradable cells. The robustness requirement (statistics.robustness_required_for_a_pass) applies to the three tradable cells only.
item_set.dropped_from_the_full_draft: Population I and its minute-trigger formulas: it is a second population with its own open finding (the listing-exchange opening print can come after decision minute m), and neither H1 nor H3 needs it. The H1 arms a_fast and c_session and their 12 cells (6 per population): they multiplied cells without adding a test of the conditioning. H1-I and the 9 I-lane cells. The holdout cap of 5 tradable cells: with three tradable cells it has no work to do, so the gate opens for every validated item. The 2017-2019 cost re-measure: it is replaced by the per-fill realized half-spread floor (cost_model.per_side), which removes a pre-outcome stage whose quote stamps were outcome prices. H2, H4 and H5 (and their data gates) and H6: deferred (README appendix).

exposure_registry.consequence: 2017-2020 is exposed at aggregate level through broad-universe development (both lanes) and the S2 headline above. Development (2017-2019) and validation (2020) are therefore screening stages only. Validation decides which items the holdout gate opens for, but a validation pass is labelled 'screened', never confirmatory. Only the prospective holdout can support a confirmatory claim. Beside each validation result, the same statistic is reported on the least-exposed slice: symbol-sessions that were not a broad-universe lane decision. Restated from broad-universe protocol.json and evaluate.py at aa6fc79 (review round 9, L-7; core/formulas.py least_exposed), a lane decision of the widest lane (descriptive_microcap, which contains every primary-lane decision) needs a raw daily bar on t with raw close >= $1, 60 prior bars that are calendar-contiguous (so neither insufficient_history nor has_gap), and a med20 (the median of raw close x raw volume over t-20 .. t-1) that is positive and >= $2,000,000; a symbol-session missing any of these is in the slice. Broad-universe's suffix exclusion needs no restatement, because every v3 event passes exclusion 2, whose pattern removes every suffix it excludes. Limitation: the bars are the event's asof = t response, not broad-universe's default-asof history. The slice is a sensitivity, not a separate test.
exposure_registry.update_rule: Every later read of data in any v3 window before the freeze is appended here with its date and purpose. No quote at a planned v3 entry or exit stamp is fetched before the freeze. The coverage-stamp quotes (pre_freeze_access_path.quote_coverage_stamps) are chosen with no reference to event membership and may fall inside a later D trade's hold or terminal-search window; only the count-only code opens them. Daily bars, official prints, quotes and the coverage-selected minute bars are fetched before the freeze only into the sealed pre_freeze_access_path snapshot, whose 2016-2020 screen part is a hashed sample, never the full screen, and are opened only by the count-only code. Any other pre-freeze read is forbidden, not tolerated. If one happens anyway, it is appended here and recorded as a numbered deviation before the freeze, and it voids this protocol version's tests: every item scores p = 1 in the validation Holm run, so the holdout never opens. A read of a v3-defined outcome in the validation window before the freeze voids validation. A read in the holdout window before the gate opens voids the holdout. In code (review round 10, F4): such a read is recorded in deviations.json as {number, kind 'void', scope, cause}, scope 'tests' (a pre-freeze read of data in any v3 window), 'validation' (a pre-freeze read of a validation-window outcome) or 'holdout' (a holdout-window read before the gate opens). core.guards.voids reads the committed records (a malformed one is refused); run.py evaluate then gives every validation item p = 1 for 'tests' or 'validation', and the evaluator refuses every 'count' and 'read' authorization under any of them, so a 'read' writes the not-read label. Review round 12, F6 of the second review: the reach of each void deviation is checked. Review round 13, F1 (Claude) and Codex P2: a void applies only if it reached origin/main before the outcome it would void could have been computed, so no void can be chosen after that outcome, or after paper results, were seen. Each void record has its own signed reach time (core.guards.void_records). A 'tests' or 'validation' void applies (every validation p = 1, so nothing is carried and the holdout never opens) only if it reached origin/main before the validation stage's first 'evaluate_start' line did (run_discipline.once: the evaluation runs in two committed steps); an applied one that reached origin/main after the freeze commit is named in results/validation.json (void.void_deviations_after_freeze), since this rule wants it recorded before the freeze. A 'holdout' void also cites the time of the read it records (read_utc, an RFC 3339 UTC stamp; a record without one is refused as malformed) and applies (count and read authorizations are refused, and a read that sealed nothing writes the not-read label) only if it reached origin/main before the holdout gate opened, which is when the first granted 'count' or 'read' authorization reached origin/main, and its read_utc is no later than its record and before the gate opened. A void that does not apply is late: it is never applied and never cancels, delays or refuses a read (chronology.holdout.read_timing); it is reported with its number, scope, reach time and reason in results/validation.json (void.void_deviations_late) when that is written after it, and in the holdout read's voids_late and holdout_label (core.runner.void_effect). Limitation: a void recorded before its bound is taken at its word; paper results exist before the gate opens, and code cannot tell a genuine pre-gate read from a claimed one, but such a void can only suppress a result, never create a supported claim.

pre_freeze_access_path.rule: Before the freeze, data are fetched only by committed count-only code in the study tree (run_discipline.study_code). Raw pages go straight into a private snapshot sealed by sha256. They are never opened by a person or by any other code. The count-only code emits only counts, rates and the coverage_rule decisions: no price, spread, return, gain, covariate value, event list or symbol-level row. Its committed output is the input to the freeze preconditions. The pre-freeze snapshot is never an input of the frozen evaluation, with one exception (review round 12, F5 of the second review): part 0's sealed enumeration (enumeration.json, whose sha256 the governing count-only output pins as part0.enumeration_sha256) is the development and validation symbol list, active set and corporate-action records up to the pre-freeze fetch date (freeze_preconditions). No price, print, quote or bar of the pre-freeze snapshot is an input: part 2 is no longer fetched before the freeze, and the holdout breakpoint screen is fetched after the freeze (snapshot_contents, review round 8, R8-3 and E2). Its 2016-2020 screen part is a hashed sample of symbol-sessions, enough for coverage rates and a candidate count, so before the freeze no complete set of inputs to any development or validation outcome (including H3-c's official prints and close-to-close proxies of b_lane) exists on disk while the draft is still editable. The full 2016-2020 screen data and every per-event request are fetched only after the freeze under run_discipline.fetch (review round 7, C4).
pre_freeze_access_path.snapshot_contents: (0) The enumerated symbol list (universe_and_identity.enumeration), with its source responses, and the corporate-action records from 2016-01-01 to the fetch date. (1) A hashed sample of 2016-2020 screen data. The pair (symbol, s) is sampled if int.from_bytes(sha256('mover-v3-sample|' + symbol + '|' + s)[:8], 'big') % 20 == 0, for every enumerated symbol and every XNYS session s from 2016-01-04 to 2020-12-31, with no reference to event membership. For each sampled pair: the daily bars (adjustment raw, split and all) and official prints (auctions, with their sessions_io.official_price source labels) of sessions s-1 and s, requested with asof = s; the same daily bars requested at the provider's default asof, for identity_diagnostic only; and, for the pairs that quote_coverage_stamps selects, the coverage-stamp quotes and the regular-session 1-minute bars of s, both requested with asof = s (the minute bars measure minute-bar coverage, review round 8, E3). No 2016-2020 screen row outside the sample is fetched before the freeze. (2) Removed (review round 8, R8-3 and E2): the 2024-11-01 to 2025-12-31 screen for the holdout breakpoints is not fetched before the freeze. It is fetched after the freeze under the first granted 'count' entry, by the frozen code with asof = s, and sealed before use (tercile_rule.holdout_breakpoints). The part numbers are kept. (3) The native identity probe of identity_probe. No other minute bar and no other quote is fetched before the freeze. Every part is pinned by sha256. Each page record keeps its request asof and its fetch date (the vintage) as separate fields.

rate_limit.rule: Review round 10, L1: the provider's documented request rate limit and its primary source, committed here (on origin/main) before the count-only run. It decides the fetch-time estimate and so fetch_margin (coverage_rule.thresholds.fetch_estimate), so run.py count-only takes it from this field only (core.count_only.pinned_rate_limit) and refuses to run while it is null. It is set by a reviewed pull request before the count-only run and is not part of coverage_rule, so its value does not change coverage_rule's sha256. Review round 11, C2: every fetching command (count-only, dry-run, fetch, transport-check, collect, count and read) refuses while per_minute is null, and passes it to the transport's child process, which paces every page request, retries included, at per_minute with one pacer for the data and trading hosts (fetch/transport.py Pacer). An HTTP 429 waits at least one full 60 s rate window before its retry instead of the 1 s, 4 s and 16 s schedule.

pre_freeze_access_path.quote_coverage_stamps: Eligible-quote rates are measured only at stamps that are never planned v3 entry or exit stamps: 12:17 ET and 14:43 ET (12:17 and 12:43 ET on a 13:00 early close). They may fall inside a later D trade's hold or terminal-search window; only the count-only code opens them. The symbol-sessions are selected among the part-1 sampled symbol-sessions with a daily bar and a raw close >= $1 by int.from_bytes(sha256('mover-v3-coverage|' + symbol + '|' + session)[:8], 'big') % 25 == 0 (about 1 in 500 overall), with no reference to event membership. A stamp has an eligible quote if the NBBO prevailing at the stamp is eligible (populations.fill_quote) and at most 1000 ms old, or if the first eligible quote update after the stamp arrives within 60 s. Per year, the code reports the stamps with an eligible quote, those without one, and those that are fetch-incomplete (populations.fetch_failures), and nothing else.
pre_freeze_access_path.runs: The count-only code runs once, from the committed study tree named in its output. Every run, including a failed or partial one, is appended to this registry with its revision, tree, date and output sha256. A rerun is allowed only after a failed or incomplete run, and never after its rates were read. The first complete run's output governs coverage_rule. The count-only code is the only code that opens parts 1 and 3. Review round 11, F4: the count-only run, the native dry run and each stage fetch run in two committed steps. The first run.py call appends only a '<purpose>_start' run-log line naming the protocol sha256, the study tree and (count-only) the coverage_rule sha256 (dry run: the sessions and the symbols' sha256) and fetches nothing; the next call runs only once that line is on origin/main, and its end line cites the start by start_index. While a start has no end line, a run with another protocol, tree, rule or session list is refused, so changing a threshold after a discarded local attempt needs a pushed end line first. Every start line is a logged exposure of this registry. Limitation: a discarded local attempt under an unchanged start can still be rerun; it reads the same requests under the same rule, and its start is logged. Review round 12, F3 of the second review: each part's sha256 is logged as soon as the part is sealed, so a failed count-only run's end line names every part it sealed (input_snapshot_sha256s and sealed_parts), and the dry run's the same. Once a failed run has sealed part 1, a later count-only run must have the same coverage_rule sha256 (run.py refuses otherwise), so the rule is never changed after its rates could have been read. Review round 15, N02 (R14-open-2): a hard kill between an output's rename and its run-log line leaves an output that no line cites. It never governs by itself, and nothing is fetched again: the next run under the open start line recomputes the output from its sealed inputs (count-only: parts 0, 1 and 3 and the enumeration file, core.count_only.output_from_sealed; dry run: its snapshot, dry_run_output), adopts the file only if it equals that recomputation on every field but the commit the killed run ran at, and writes its complete line with adopted_uncited_output true (core.runner.adopt_uncited_output). A file that does not reproduce is refused. A file that a line cites refuses a second run, as before.
pre_freeze_access_path.not_allowed: No pre-freeze fetch or read of a quote at a planned D entry or exit stamp. No pre-freeze fetch of 2016-2020 screen rows outside the part-1 sample. No opening of the sealed snapshot's bars, prints or quotes by a person or by code other than the count-only code. No computation of D membership (the candidate count stops before DV_reg), MAX21 or any outcome.
pre_freeze_access_path.identity_diagnostic: A count-only measure of what asof = s screening cannot reach (review round 7, F4). A part-1 sampled pair (X, s) is identity-unreached if X's default-asof response has a daily bar for s with a raw close >= $1 whose raw OHLCV differs from X's asof = s row, or X has no asof = s row, and no retained name_change record names X as its new symbol. Such a history belongs to an issuer that carried another ticker on s, and asof = s screening reaches it only through that old ticker, which neither enumeration source holds when no rename record was retained. broad-universe, which requested the default asof, received such histories under the successor ticker. Per year, the code reports the sampled pairs with a default-asof bar and raw close >= $1, the identity-unreached pairs and their rate, and the distinct unreached symbols. The rate is an upper bound (an old ticker can still be in the asset master). It enters coverage_rule.year_rule and chronology.labels.validation.
pre_freeze_access_path.identity_probe: A count-only native check of the asof = t behaviour that universe_and_identity.asof relies on, for 2016-2020 (review round 7, F5). The list is fixed by rule: every name_change record of part 0 effective (process_date, universe_and_identity.corporate_action_dates) on a session d from 2016-01-04 to 2020-12-31 (old symbol O, new symbol N), ordered by sha256('mover-v3-probe|' + O + '|' + N + '|' + d) and capped at the first 100. For each, the code requests O with asof = d-3 and N with asof = d+3 (sessions), each over sessions d-3 .. d+3, for daily bars (raw), auctions and quotes (the 60 s ending 12:17 ET on d-1 and on d+1). A rename probe matches on an endpoint if both responses are complete and hold exactly the same sessions, at least one before d and one on or after d, with identical raw daily OHLCV (or auction prints) on every one of them, and for quotes if both windows of both sides are complete, non-empty and identical update for update (review round 15, F09: before, one common session was enough, and two merely non-empty quote responses matched). Ticker reuse is probed on every symbol that is the old symbol of one name_change record and the new symbol of a later one inside 2016-2020 (same order, capped at 50): requested for a session before the first record, once with asof before the first record and once with asof after the second. Review round 15, N07: a case is verified when the early response has the old issuer's bar and the late one has none or a different one; it is an observed failure when the late response returns the identical bar; it is inconclusive when a request is fetch-incomplete or the early response has no bar. Only match and mismatch counts per endpoint are emitted. The freeze needs at least 20 rename probes, at least 95% matches for bars and for auctions and at least 90% for quotes, and no observed ticker-reuse failure (ticker_reuse_failed_cases_max = 0; review round 15, N07) (coverage_rule.thresholds.identity_probe, hashed, review round 8, R8-9); otherwise the protocol is not frozen as written. The count-only code emits the pass or fail. If no reuse case exists, or none is conclusive, the ticker-reuse claim of universe_and_identity.asof is recorded as unverified for 2016-2020 (the zero-case policy: it does not fail the gate, and the output reports the listed, verified, failed and inconclusive case counts). In code (review round 12, F2 of the second review): core.runner.check_coverage_decision refuses every command under a frozen protocol whose governing count-only output does not have identity_probe.passes and fetch_margin.passes true, or whose rate_limit differs from this protocol's pre_freeze_access_path.rate_limit, so no threshold is applied by hand.

exposure_registry.collection_limitation: Review round 10, L2: the sealed pre-freeze snapshots and the holdout collection batches are plain gzip pages under a snapshot root the operator chooses. That no person opens them before the gate is procedural only. A collection batch holds the raw, split and all daily bars and official prints of the whole enumerated list for every collected holdout session, which is enough for close-to-close proxies of b_lane before the read. Collection is not a read (chronology.holdout.holdout_read), so no code stops such a look; the batches are neither encrypted nor withheld, and this limitation stands. Review round 12, F4 of the second review: the same holds for the sealed holdout count snapshots. A count fetches and seals, for every holdout event, the per-event raw, split and all daily bars, the official prints (every open and close from d1 to d5, the complete inputs of H3-c's holdout outcome) and the 1-minute bars from t-19 through the close of E+5, before any read is authorized. The count code computes only count_unit from them, but keeping people out of that snapshot is procedural only.

universe_and_identity.enumeration: The symbol list for 2016-2020 is the union of two sources (the 2024-11-01 to 2025-12-31 breakpoint screen enumerates from the same two sources at the first granted 'count', review round 8, R8-3). (a) The Alpaca asset master: GET /v2/assets with status=active and with status=inactive, class us_equity, every current exchange including OTC (today's OTC listing says nothing about 2016-2020 listing, which exclusions rule 1 decides from session data). Symbols that fail collect_daily.py DATA_SYMBOL at aa6fc79 (CUSIP-style placeholders the bars API rejects) are removed. (b) Every symbol named by an Alpaca corporate-action record (GET /v1/corporate-actions, every action type, 2016-01-01 to the fetch date) in any symbol field core/records.py keeps: symbol, old_symbol, new_symbol, acquirer_symbol, acquiree_symbol, target_symbol, source_symbol and new_symbol_2 (review round 10, F11). DATA_SYMBOL filters (b) too, as collect_daily.py at aa6fc79 filtered its supplement list, since the bars API rejects such placeholders. This is broad-universe's supplement method (collect_daily.py and corporate_actions.py at aa6fc79), except that renamed-away tickers are kept, because per-session asof resolves them. The list is written once, sealed with the pre-freeze snapshot and pinned by sha256, and its per-source counts are count-only outputs (core.identity.enumerate_symbols). Survivorship limit: a name delisted in 2016-2019 that is absent from both sources cannot be discovered (broad-universe/README.md: 'names delisted in 2016-2019 without a retained action cannot be discovered from entitled sources'), so development keeps the survivorship-limited label. A second limit concerns identity: an issuer renamed without a retained name_change record, whose old ticker is in neither source, is not reached for its pre-rename sessions by asof = s screening, although broad-universe, which requested the provider's default asof, received that history under the successor ticker (113 of its 155 duplicate pairs were resolved without a rename record, and name_change records number 57 for 2017-2019; broad-universe/README.md). exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path.identity_diagnostic measures it per year, and coverage_rule.year_rule and chronology.labels.validation use it. Holdout collection batches enumerate from the same two sources, refreshed at each batch, united with every earlier batch's list.
universe_and_identity.asof: Every request for bars, auctions (official prints) or quotes carries Alpaca's asof parameter set to a session date, never to the fetch date and never to the provider default. A screen request for session s uses asof = s. Every request for a D event decided on session t uses the event's as-known symbol with asof = t. The as-known symbol is the one under which the event appeared in the asof = t screen. Such requests cover the event's daily bars (raw, split and all) from t-60 (t-22 for a holdout event; review round 9, L-5) through the end of its terminal-search window, its minute bars, its entry, exit and terminal-search quotes and its official prints through the end of its hold or search window. A rename inside a hold or lookback is therefore resolved to the same issuer. The fetch date is kept as a separate vintage field in each page record. quotes.py fetch_one, whose PROTOCOL_ASOF is fixed at '2026-09-21', is never called.
universe_and_identity.request_shapes: The screen data are: for 2016-2020, the full screen fetch made after the freeze (run_discipline.fetch: daily bars raw, split and all, and official prints of sessions s-1 and s for the whole enumerated list, with asof = s, sealed and pinned before any outcome); for 2024-11 to 2025-12, the breakpoint screen fetched under the first granted 'count' with asof = s and sealed before use (review round 8, R8-3); and for the holdout, the collection batches. The pre-freeze sample is never a screen input. The gain condition (close[t], ref(t), f(t)), the $1 floor, suspected unadjusted splits at t and exclusions 1 and 2 are evaluated on the screen data. Only the symbol-sessions that pass them are candidates, and only candidates have per-event data fetched, with the as-known symbol and asof = t. Per-event data are: the minute bars for DV_reg (the last membership condition), med20, the entry bar and cum_dv; the event's daily bars with adjustment raw, split and all, one request per adjustment, from t-60 (t-22 for exclusion 3 and MAX21; t-60 for the least-exposed slice of exposure_registry.consequence, a validation sensitivity; a holdout event starts at t-22, so for a decision on N0 - 1 or later its lookback begins after the freeze session and never enters #162's reserved window, review round 9, L-5) through the scheduled close of the 5th session after its latest planned exit session (for a censored trade, after the segment's last session; populations.terminal_exits); the official prints from t-22 over the same sessions; the minute bars from 04:00 ET of t-19 through the same scheduled close; and quote windows. The quote windows and their order are fixed in core/plan.py (review round 8, R8-1): entry [X - 1 s, X + 300 s]; exit W0 = [X - 1 s, min(X + 300 s, close of E)], W1 = [X + 300 s, close of E] when X + 300 s is before the close, then one full regular session per session E+1 .. E+5, each requested only when every earlier window of that exit is complete and holds no fill; and the backward windows of populations.terminal_exits.booking. The per-event daily bars supply MAX21, exclusion 3, every in-hold share factor and the D7 cash term (populations.corporate_actions), each computed within that event's responses only; screen rows, fetched under other symbols, asof values and vintages, are never joined into a per-event computation (review round 7, F1). If a per-event official close of t or t-1 differs from the screen value, the screen value governs membership, and the difference is counted per stage.
universe_and_identity.dedup: Before membership, coverage.dedupe_identity at aa6fc79 (its byte-for-byte pinned copy, run through DuckDB: the screen table is loaded into the table joined with the schema symbol VARCHAR, session_date DATE, raw_o, raw_h, raw_l, raw_c, raw_v DOUBLE, one row per symbol and session s from its asof = s request; duckdb is pinned in study/runtime.lock, review round 8, E1) (DUPLICATE_SERIES_MIN_SESSIONS = 20, DUPLICATE_SERIES_MIN_SPAN_COVERAGE = 0.98, survivor ranking by retained rename record, then price continuity, then active status, then lexicographic order) is applied as of each candidate session t (review round 12, Codex P1): for a candidate (symbol, t) it runs on the screen rows of sessions <= t only, each from its asof = s request, so no row after t (a close inside the candidate's own hold window, a later rename, a later last trading day or price continuity after t) can decide whether the candidate at t is a member. It runs on the rows of the symbols linked to the candidate's symbol by a byte-identical raw OHLCV row (volume > 0) on some session <= t, which is exact, because dedupe_identity decides each component of qualified pairs from its members' rows only (core.identity.dedupe_asof). Dedup filters candidates; the per-reason screen counts are over the screen rows before dedup. There is also a same-session guard. Two candidate D events on one session whose raw daily OHLCV (volume > 0) is identical on both s-1 and s are one event, kept under the higher-ranked symbol (for this guard: the retained-rename terminus, then lexicographic order, as of the session (review round 13, F2; active status was dropped); price continuity is not used because both rows are identical). Because the rows are identical, the choice cannot change any price up to the session; the forward quotes may differ, which is why the choice uses nothing known after it. Candidates removed by either rule are counted per stage (dedupe_candidates_removed and same_session_guard_removed). Review round 13, F2: the survivor of two duplicate tickers at t books the trade's entry, exit and terminal-search quotes, so both rules decide it as of t: they use only the name_change records effective (process_date) on or before t (a record without a date is never used), and no active status, because the asset master is today's, not as of t; the active-status step of dedupe_identity's ranking is therefore never reached, and the same-session guard ranks by the rename terminus, then lexicographic order (core.identity.rename_records, pairs_asof). A rename or delisting after t cannot choose which ticker's forward quotes fill or book a terminal zero. Review round 14, F4: 'the screen rows of sessions <= t' are the rows of the candidate's own stage screen (core.stage.StageSpec.screen_sessions): development 2016-01-04 onward, validation from the last kept 2019 session, and the holdout's 2024-11-01 .. 2025-12-31 breakpoint screen and N0 - 1 onward. Rows of an earlier stage, and the unscreened holdout gap 2026-01-02 .. N0 - 2, are never joined, so a duplicate pair qualifies (DUPLICATE_SERIES_MIN_SESSIONS = 20 shared sessions) only on rows inside the stage's screen, and in about the first 20 sessions of validation and of each holdout screen part a duplicate pair can stay unqualified. The same-session guard still removes identical twin candidates there. Feeding a stage the screen rows of another stage was not adopted: it would join snapshots sealed for another window into a stage's membership.
universe_and_identity.empty_responses: HTTP 200 with no row is an empty response, never silently dropped, and never fetch-incomplete (fetch-incomplete is reserved for HTTP errors and timeouts, populations.fetch_failures). Per stage, the counts reported are: enumerated symbols with no bar in the stage; screen requests with no row; and, per item, event requests with no row. Each empty event request has a fixed consequence. An empty entry-quote window is a no-entry. An empty exit or search window is a terminal exit (populations.terminal_exits), which stays in the statistic. An empty official-print response is a missing print: no event at t, or a missing H3-c leg. An empty lookback makes MAX21 undefined, so the event is unassigned. An empty minute-bar response gives DV_reg 0 (not an event); candidates with daily volume > 0 and no regular-session minute bar are reported per stage (review round 8, E3). In code (review round 11, C6): counts.empty_by_item reports, per computed item over its trades of every status (H3-c: its events), the per-event requests with no row by kind and the entry windows, exit windows (on the planned exit session) and search windows (E+1 .. E+5) with no row. Review round 11, C7: a synthetic test checks that a per-event official close of t or t-1 that differs from the screen's is counted in per_event_close_differs_from_screen and leaves the event unchanged (request_shapes).
universe_and_identity.tests: Synthetic tests with a recorded fake client cover: FB/META (a renamed-away ticker served with its successor's history under both symbols gives one event, not two); a ticker reused by a new issuer after a delisting (asof = t resolves the old issuer); a rename inside a 5-session hold (the as-known symbol with asof = t returns the whole hold); a split and a rename inside the same hold (the share factor and the cash term come from the per-event responses under the as-known symbol, never from screen rows); an empty exit response (a terminal exit, counted); and a request built with the fetch date as asof (refused).
universe_and_identity.corporate_action_dates: Review round 8, E7. A corporate-action record is effective on the session named by one field per type: name_change process_date; forward_split, reverse_split, unit_split, stock_dividend and cash_dividend ex_date; cash_merger, stock_merger and stock_and_cash_merger effective_date; any other type process_date. The identity probe, the in-hold split-record exclusion, terminal-merger booking, the terminal-zero rename count and the holdout rename re-fetch all use this field (core/records.py). The response envelope's type keys are accepted in the singular and the plural. Review round 15, N02 (R14-open-1): a holdout count and a read each fetch their own terminal-record request (kind terminal_actions: every corporate action from 2016-01-01 to their own fetch date; a read is fetched after the last terminal-search window has ended), and the trade walk uses its records together with the enumeration's: terminal-merger booking, the in-hold split-record exclusion and the rename sensitivity. Its records never enter the enumeration, the screen or the dedup, which keep the first count's corporate-action request, so the enumerated symbols and the screen plan do not change. The '_fetch' line records terminal_actions_fetch_date, and the evaluation step rebuilds the same plan from it.

populations.D_daily: Symbol-sessions t with split-consistent official-close gain close[t]/ref(t) - 1 >= 0.20 - 1e-9, where close[t] is the accepted official close of populations.official_prints and ref(t) is as populations.formulas states. They also need an official close >= $1.00 and a regular-session dollar volume DV_reg(t) >= $1,000,000. A session without an accepted official close is not an event and is counted; there is no bar fallback. The decision is at 16:15 ET on t. Entry is at the first eligible quote at or after 09:35 ET on t+1 (and at or after decision + 60 s), with an entry timeout of 300 s; otherwise there is no entry, and it is counted. The b_overnight entry is the exception (arms.b_overnight).
populations.formulas: Restated exactly, so membership does not depend on unpinned code. Let a(s) = raw daily close(s) / split-adjusted daily close(s), the cumulative split factor of session s, from the daily bars with adjustment=raw and adjustment=split. For sessions u < v, the share factor F(u, v) = a(u) / a(v), set to 1 when |F - 1| <= 1e-2. F(u, v) is undefined if u or v has no daily bar in either adjustment, and every quantity that uses an undefined F is undefined (counted). F telescopes, so a split that takes effect on a session with no bar (for example, halted all day) is still carried between the surrounding sessions with bars. f(j) = F(j-1, j) for consecutive XNYS sessions. This is rules.split_factor's arithmetic at aa6fc79 with two deliberate departures: adjustment=split closes replace adjustment=all closes (with adjustment=all, a cash dividend of about 1% or more would be booked as a share change), and a missing input makes F undefined instead of 1 (a default of 1 left a split on a session without a bar unbooked, review round 7 F2). ref(t) = the accepted official close of the previous XNYS session / f(t). If that session has no accepted official close, or f(t) is undefined, ref(t) is undefined and t is not an event (counted). DV_reg(t) = the summed vwap x volume of the 1-minute SIP bars of session t that start at or after 09:30 ET and before the scheduled close (session_calendar); a session with no such bar has DV_reg 0. The split-consistent official-close return of session j is r(j) = C(j) x f(j) / C(j-1) - 1, where C is the accepted official close; r(j) is undefined if either close is missing or f(j) is undefined. MAX21(t) = the maximum over k = 1..21 of r(t-k). These are the 21 returns of sessions t-21 .. t-1, from the 22 accepted official closes of sessions t-22 .. t-1 (the event's own session t is not in the window). If any of those closes is missing, or any session t-21 .. t-1 is a suspected unadjusted split, MAX21 is undefined and the event is unassigned (counted); there is no maximum over fewer returns. The sizing window W(t) is the 20 sessions ending at t (its close is known at the 16:15 decision). med20 = the median of DV_reg over W(t). sigma_d = the sample standard deviation (ddof = 1) of log(1 + r(j)) over the 20 sessions j of W(t). If any DV_reg or r(j) in W(t) is undefined, the trade cannot be sized and is a counted no-fill. The entry bar is the last 1-minute SIP bar of the entry session (from 04:00 ET) that is complete at the fill-decision time X, meaning it starts at or before X - 60 s. If there is none, the entry-bar cap is 0 and the trade is a counted no-fill. A synthetic test fixes each formula, including a split day, a missing previous close, a missing close inside the MAX21 window, a suspected unadjusted split inside it, a reverse split on a session with no daily bar inside a lookback (MAX21 undefined) and inside a hold (carried by F between the surrounding bars), and an entry with no completed bar. Review round 11, C10: a 1-minute bar whose vwap is missing or zero takes its close as vwap (core/records.py and the pinned rules.Bars.from_rows at aa6fc79 both do this), so DV_reg, med20, cum_dv and the entry-bar cap use close x volume for such a bar. This is the pinned code's behaviour and is stated here, not a fallback chosen for v3.
populations.official_prints: The accepted source labels of sessions_io.official_price at aa6fc79 are these. The listing exchange is the exchange of the largest condition-O opening print; a session with no O print has no listing exchange. Official open: opening_print_listing_exchange only. Official close: closing_print_listing_exchange or official_close_listing_exchange only. A closing_print_other_exchange, or a session with no O print, counts as no official close and is counted per year. The same rule applies to close[t], to the previous close in ref(t) and to every H3-c leg. For D, the O print of session t precedes the 16:15 ET decision by construction. The synthetic suite has one case per source label, including the rejected label and a session with a closing print but no opening print.
populations.suspected_unadjusted_split: Applied at t before membership, on the screen data. For session t, let r = raw daily close[t] / raw daily close of the previous XNYS session. Session t is a suspected unadjusted split if f(t) = 1 and |r - n| <= 0.01 x n or |r - 1/n| <= 0.01 / n for some integer n in 2..100. Such a session is not an event, and any event whose MAX21 window (t-21 .. t-1) contains a suspected session is unassigned; both are counted per stage. The rule also removes genuine moves at t within 1% of an integer multiple (for example +100%); that loss is preregistered and counted, not corrected. Inside a hold the ratio rule is never applied to a primary statistic: hold-period close ratios are outcomes, and the rule would drop real tail moves of low-priced movers (+100%, +200%, -50%, -67%). A trade is excluded from the primary statistics only on price-independent evidence: a retained forward_split or reverse_split record effective (ex_date, universe_and_identity.corporate_action_dates) on a session j with entry session < j <= planned exit session while F(entry session, planned exit session) = 1, so the adjusted bars do not carry the recorded split. That exclusion uses only records and the cumulative factors a(s) (ratios of two closes of one session, never a return), so count_unit applies it too; it is counted per item and stage. Removing trades whose hold spans a session flagged by the ratio rule is a sensitivity only (statistics.sensitivities; review round 7, C3). Review round 15, N06: a delayed exit holds the position past the planned exit session E (up to E+5), so for a trade that fills after E the same record exclusions (the split record with F = 1, and the spin-off record of populations.corporate_actions) are applied through the actual exit session: a record effective in (entry session, x] while F(entry session, x) = 1 excludes it (core.trades.record_exclusion). count_unit, which never sees the exit, applies them through E.
populations.exclusions: (1) Not exchange-listed on the session: a symbol-session is eligible only if it has a listing exchange under populations.official_prints, so OTC-only trading is excluded by as-known session data. The current Alpaca asset exchange and tradable flags are never used. (2) Warrants, units and rights: exclude the symbol if (len(symbol) == 5 and re.search('[A-Z]{4}[WUR]$', symbol)) or re.search('\.(WS|U|R|W)', symbol) (Python re, unanchored search), which is candidates.py's rule at aa6fc79 (its SQL regexp_matches, line 47), or if the symbol contains '/', a v3 addition that candidates.py does not have. (3) Fewer than 21 of the 22 sessions t-22 .. t-1 have a raw daily bar in the event's per-event response (review round 8, E8: the window is the per-event lookback, not the symbol's whole history). Each exclusion is counted per stage, with a synthetic test per rule. There is no halt exclusion (halts). Exclusion 1 is checked first, before the accepted-close check: a session with no listing exchange has no accepted close, so a later check could never fire. Its count is the symbol-sessions with a bar and no listing-exchange opening print (review round 9, M-7).
populations.fetch_failures: The frozen request plan and records are v3-owned evaluation code (core/plan.py, core/store.py); study/fetch/ only moves bytes. Records use quotes.py's page and completion format at aa6fc79 (a stamp_complete or stamp_incomplete record per request, now for every request kind, with the kind named). Every page request is retried up to 3 times, waiting 1 s, 4 s and 16 s. A request that still fails with an HTTP error, a URLError or a timeout is fetch-incomplete; the run continues and does not raise. Consequences by kind (review round 8, R8-5 and E5): a screen batch (daily bars or auctions of one session for one batch of symbols) makes every symbol-session of the batch membership-unknown, excluded and counted; a per-event minute-bar or raw daily-bar request makes the candidate membership-unknown, excluded and counted; a per-event split or all daily-bar request or print request excludes the event from every item (trades and H3-c), counted per item; an entry or exit quote window excludes that trade, counted per item, and is never a no-entry or a terminal exit; a backward window excludes the trade only when a merger record needs the last bid (otherwise it removes the trade from the terminal-zero rebooking sensitivity only); a rename-sensitivity window affects that sensitivity only. HTTP 200 with no row is never fetch-incomplete (universe_and_identity.empty_responses). The stage rate is fetch-incomplete requests / all requests the stage's plan required, over every kind, after the single re-fetch of run_discipline.fetch, and is reported by kind. If it exceeds 1%, that stage is void: every item scores p = 1 and is labelled underpowered there, with the reason stated. The rate is committed in the run log before any outcome of the stage, and a void is final. Synthetic tests cover an exhausted URLError and a timeout (each becomes stamp_incomplete, and the pool run completes), a success on the third retry, an empty response (not fetch-incomplete), a failed screen batch and a failed per-event request.
populations.session_calendar: XNYS from exchange_calendars 4.13.2 (the version rules.py used for 2021-2026), from 2015-09-01 (the t-60 lookbacks of the first 2016 sessions) through the end of the last possible holdout extension. The session list, with each session's scheduled open and close, is written to the v3 data file data/session-calendar.json by data-tools/generate_session_calendar.py (its inputs and a byte-identical regeneration are pinned in data-pins.json) and pinned by sha256 at the freeze (run_discipline.data_files). Review round 15, N01: the study reads that file in its own schema (schema_version 1: a header and columns [session, open_et, close_et, open_utc, close_utc, early_close], one row per session); core.calendar.Calendar.from_document refuses any other schema and checks every row (its ET and UTC instants equal, a 09:30 ET open, a 16:00 ET close or a 13:00 ET close on a row flagged early_close) and the header's first_session, last_session, session_count and early_close_count against the rows, and core.calendar.check_study_reach refuses a calendar that does not reach 60 sessions before 2016-01-04 (the t-60 lookback of the first warm-up event) before any count-only, dry-run, fetch or evaluation. core.calendar.build_calendar writes the same schema for the synthetic tests, and a test compares its rows with the committed file's. A 'session' anywhere in this protocol is every scheduled XNYS trading session, early closes included. The pinned file cannot know about unscheduled future closures, such as a national day of mourning. Such a closure is removed only by a line in data/session-calendar-amendments.jsonl (run_discipline.amendment_format) that cites its primary source (an NYSE notice) and names a session of the pinned calendar, is committed and pushed, and is logged in the access log (purpose 'amend') before the affected session. The evaluator refuses a line that became reachable from origin/main (the GitHub-recorded time) at or after 09:30 ET of the session it removes (review round 8, R8-10). It may concern only a date on or after the freeze session. The freeze session and N0 keep the dates computed at the freeze, and if N0 itself closes, the holdout starts at the next session. The 252-session holdout and each 63-session block count actual sessions. Synthetic tests use the 2017-07-03, 2017-11-24, 2018-11-23, 2019-12-24 and 2020-11-27 early closes and a removed session inside the holdout. In code (review round 10, F2): run.py authorize --purpose amend appends the 'amend' authorization; once it is on origin/main, run.py amend --authorization ID --file calendar|fees --line N appends its completion, which cites the file, the line index, the line's sha256 and its primary source. core.runner.context refuses every other run while an amendment line has no such record, or while the record reached origin/main at or after the line's deadline (09:30 ET of the session it removes).
populations.session_times: Every '15:55 ET' in this protocol means the scheduled close (session_calendar) minus 5 minutes (12:55 ET on a 13:00 early close). Eligible quotes are regular-session quotes, at or after 09:30 ET and before the scheduled close. D decisions stay at 16:15 ET on early-close sessions.
populations.fill_quote: For a fill at or after time X, the quote is the NBBO prevailing at X (the latest quote update stamped at or before X) if it is eligible and X minus its timestamp is at most 1000 ms. Otherwise it is the first eligible quote update stamped after X, with the fill time equal to its timestamp. Eligible means bid > 0 and ask > bid (locked and crossed quotes excluded, as quotes.py valid_quote at aa6fc79 does; its pinned copy is applied only as a predicate to one quote at a time, never to a quote list, where it would skip newer locked or crossed quotes and return an older one) and regular session (session_times). Timeouts run from X. Synthetic tests cover a fresh prevailing quote, a stale one, a locked one and no quote inside the timeout. Quote updates are ordered by their exact nanosecond timestamp, as an integer, in the provider's order for identical stamps; a price never decides which of two updates is later (review round 12, Codex P2: a float epoch resolves only about 240 ns, so updates a few nanoseconds apart were reordered by price and an older eligible quote could fill after a newer locked one). A synthetic test orders two updates 9 ns apart. Review round 13, Codex P2: identical updates inside one page are all kept, in the provider's order; only a repeat of one update across a page boundary (the next page's first update identical to the previous page's last) is kept once, so [eligible A, locked B, eligible A] on one stamp leaves A prevailing (core.records.merge_quotes).
populations.fill_price: Every entry and non-terminal exit fills at the mid (bid + ask) / 2 of the eligible quote that fills it, so gross returns are mid to mid. cost_model.per_side adds the per-side cost on top.

terminal_exits.search_window: An exit fills at the first eligible quote at or after its planned stamp. If none arrives before the scheduled close, the search continues session by session through the scheduled close of the 5th XNYS session after the planned exit session E (E+5). For a trade censored at a segment end, E is the segment's last session (segment_end). A fill inside the window is a normal exit, flagged delayed and counted.
terminal_exits.terminal: A held position with no eligible quote in its search window is terminal. This covers a delisting, a move to OTC-only trading (outside the SIP NBBO), an SEC trading suspension, a halt that does not resume inside the window, and an exit request answered empty (universe_and_identity.empty_responses).
terminal_exits.booking: Terminal-merger: if a retained corporate-action record (at the holdout, one of the read's own terminal records, universe_and_identity.corporate_action_dates) of type cash_merger, stock_merger or stock_and_cash_merger names the held as-known symbol as the acquiree (its acquiree symbol field) and is effective (effective_date) on a session from the entry session through the end of the search window, the exit is booked at the last eligible bid of the hold. That is the bid of the latest eligible quote stamped after the entry fill and at or before the planned exit stamp, and merger arbitrage keeps it near the consideration. It is found in backward windows (review round 8, R8-7): for every trade whose forward search found no eligible quote, one window per session from the planned exit session back to the entry session, [max(open, entry fill), min(close, planned exit stamp)], each requested in the same sealed stage fetch only when every later window is complete and holds no eligible quote after the entry fill. If none exists, a merger trade books terminal-zero, counted as merger-without-bid. Fees are charged on that raw bid, with no further spread cost and no impact (populations.corporate_actions gives the formula). A record in which the held symbol is only the acquirer does not qualify. Terminal-zero: every other terminal trade is booked at an exit value of 0, a total loss of the position, with no exit fees. This is the stated choice. Booking at the last eligible bid for all terminal trades is a sensitivity only. Corporate-action records are thin before 2020 (broad-universe/README.md), so a merger without a retained record books terminal-zero; per stage and year, terminal-zero trades with no merger record of any kind for the symbol are reported beside the merger-record counts. Terminal-zero trades that have a retained name_change record for the held symbol (as old symbol, process_date in (entry session, E+5]) are reported as their own count, and a sensitivity re-requests their exit windows under the new symbol (asof = the rename session) and reports whether an eligible quote exists there (review round 8, E9). In the rebooking sensitivity (statistics.sensitivities), a terminal-zero trade with an eligible last bid whose share factor or cash term at the bid's session is undefined has no rebooked value: like any undefined factor it is excluded from that sensitivity and counted (terminal_zero_rebooked_undefined_factor_n), never booked at the primary -1 (review round 12, Codex P2). A terminal-zero trade with no eligible bid stays at -1 there.
terminal_exits.in_statistics: Terminal trades stay in every primary statistic, in count_unit and in the minimum samples. For each item and stage, the counts of delayed, terminal-merger and terminal-zero exits are reported. H3-c has no position: an event whose hold loses a leg this way lacks its 8 legs, is excluded from H3-c, and is counted as terminal in H3-c's report.
terminal_exits.segment_end: A trade censored at a segment end (chronology.boundaries) exits at the first eligible quote at or after its censoring stamp, 15:55 ET on the segment's last session. If none arrives before that session's scheduled close, the search continues past the segment end under the normal rule, through the scheduled close of the 5th XNYS session after the segment's last session, with the event's as-known symbol and asof = t. Quotes after the segment end are this trade's exit data only; they create no entry and no event. A fill there is flagged censored-delayed. With no eligible quote by then, the trade is terminal under the same booking and flagged censored-terminal. Where a segment ends therefore never by itself books a -100% (review round 7, C11).
terminal_exits.tests: Synthetic tests: a delisting inside a 5-session hold (terminal-zero); a delisting on a segment's last session (censored-terminal); a censored trade whose first eligible quote comes on the session after the segment end (censored-delayed); a halt that resumes on E+3 (delayed exit); a halt that has not resumed by E+5 (terminal-zero); a cash merger effective inside the hold (terminal-merger at the last eligible bid); an empty exit response; and a check that each case is counted and kept in the statistic.

populations.corporate_actions: For every arm and each H3-c leg, deviation D7's method (evaluate_v2.py lines 416-420 at aa6fc79) is restated with its cash clamp. Let e be the entry session and x the exit session (the session of the exit fill, or of the terminal-merger bid), N = filled notional / entry mid the entry shares, and raw_c and all_c the adjustment=raw and adjustment=all daily closes. Every input comes from the event's per-event daily-bar responses (universe_and_identity.request_shapes), never from screen rows. The share factor is F = F(e, x) (populations.formulas), and exit shares are N x F. The cash term covers the ex-dates in (e, x] for every arm, including b_overnight (e = t+1, x = t+2) and each overnight H3-c leg (e = t+k, x = t+k+1), each dividend taken at the close of the session immediately before its ex-date (review round 14, Codex P2; follow-up review of 202968f, Codex P2). Let split_c be the adjustment=split daily close and D(d) = all_c(d) / split_c(d) the dividend-only adjustment of session d. For consecutive sessions p < k of [e, x] that both have split and all bars, s_k = 1 - D(p) / D(k); a step with |s_k| <= 2e-3 is adjustment-rounding noise and books nothing. A session of [e, x] without its split or all bar is not skipped: a step outside that band between two such sessions p and k that are not consecutive XNYS sessions cannot name the ex-date or the close immediately before it, so the cash is undefined; a step inside the band across a missing session books nothing, as anywhere else (follow-up review of 202968f, Codex P2: with closes $20, $40, $39, $39, $39 over e .. x, a $1 dividend ex on the third session and only the second session's split bar missing, skipping that session priced the dividend at the $20 close of e and booked $0.50 instead of $1). Then cash = a(e) x the sum of split_c(p) x s_k per original share, a(e) = raw_c(e) / split_c(e) (populations.formulas), and cash = cash if |cash| > 2e-3 x raw_c(e) else 0.0, booked with its sign (review round 8, E6: D7's one-sided 1e-4 clamp credited positive adjustment-rounding noise of up to about 6e-4 and zeroed negative noise; the symmetric band above the measured noise removes that bias). The cash is undefined, and the trade or H3-c event excluded and counted like an undefined F, without the raw, split and all bars of e and x, or when a dividend's previous close is missing as above. Review round 14, Codex P2: D7's cash = raw_c(e) x all_c(x) / all_c(e) - F x raw_c(x) scaled each dividend by the close of x, so an exit at the open of x (b_overnight, the overnight H3-c legs) booked cash that moved with x's later intraday return (entry close $20, a $1 dividend ex on x, exit at x's open: cash 1 with x's close at 19, 2 with it at 38); the per-ex-date form uses no price after the previous close of each ex-date and equals D7's when the price does not move. For a same-session trade or leg (a_intraday, the intraday H3-c legs) e = x, so F = 1 and cash = 0. The trade net return is net = (N x F x exit_mid x (1 - c_out) - sell_fees + N x cash) / (N x entry_mid x (1 + c_in)) - 1, where c_in and c_out are the entry and exit costs of cost_model.per_side (fractions of the mid, impact included) and sell_fees is the dollar SEC Section 31 fee and FINRA TAF on selling N x F shares at the raw exit mid: rate x sell value / 1e6 + min(TAF per share x N x F, TAF max per trade), unrounded (cost_model.fees; no fee on the buy, and commission 0; review round 8, R8-12). A terminal-merger exit uses exit_mid = the last eligible bid and c_out = 0, with fees on that bid. A terminal-zero trade has net = -1 exactly (no exit value, fees or cash). H3-c legs are gross: an overnight leg is log((raw official open(x) x F + cash) / raw official close(e)), and an intraday leg is log(raw official close / raw official open) of one session. An undefined F excludes the trade, or the H3-c event, and is counted. Mergers follow populations.terminal_exits. Synthetic tests, passed before the freeze, fix the net-return formula on a small table and cross a split, an ordinary ex-dividend date, a special cash dividend of 5% (booked as cash with F = 1, never as a share change, and not flagged as a suspected unadjusted split), a cash term inside the band (5e-4 noise of either sign books 0), a split effective on the exit session of b_overnight, a split followed by a dividend inside the hold, a missing bar inside the hold (booked when no step outside the band crosses it, undefined when one does, including the non-flat $20, $40, $39 case above), and an exit at the open of the ex-date whose cash does not change with that session's close (review round 14). Review round 15, F01 (supported entitlements and spin-offs): the cash term books cash distributions only, ordinary and special cash dividends and any other cash distribution the provider's all adjustment carries, each at the close before its ex-date. A spin-off's entitlement is shares of another issuer, which the cash term would book as cash at the provider's adjustment value; so a trade whose hold, or an H3-c event whose sessions t+1 .. t+5, span the ex-date of a retained spin_off record of the held symbol (its source_symbol; effective on its ex_date, universe_and_identity.corporate_action_dates) in (entry session, exit session] (for H3-c, (t+1, t+5]) is excluded and counted as spin_off_record_excluded, in the count and the read alike (core.trades.record_exclusion). Limitation: a spin-off or other non-cash distribution (rights, a stock dividend outside the split adjustment) without a retained record cannot be told from a cash distribution in the adjustment factors, and is booked as cash at its adjustment value (tests/test_trades.py Round15Accounting pins this).
populations.halts: No halt source is used, historically or prospectively, so no trade set depends on a later data purchase. As in catalyst-experiment, a halt is never inferred from missing data. An entry fills only at an eligible quote, and an entry with none inside its timeout is a counted no-entry. An exit waits for an eligible quote and becomes terminal after its search window (populations.terminal_exits). Limitation: a trade that sits through a short unobserved halt is not flagged.
populations.parameter_provenance: G = 0.20 and V = $1M are v1's loosest gain and middle volume floor. They were fixed for sample size after v1's all-negative dev/val grid was seen (a disclosed exposure) and are not tuned on any v3 window.

arms.b_lane: H1: entry as D_daily; exit at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on the 5th holding session (the entry session t+1 is holding session 1), under populations.terminal_exits
arms.a_intraday: H3-a: entry as D_daily (09:35 ET on t+1, timeout 300 s); exit at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on the entry session. Its entries are the b_lane entries of all D events, assigned or unassigned to a tercile. The overlap is intended and reported (counts.a_intraday_b_lane_entry_overlap: filled H3-a trades, and those whose event also has a filled b_lane trade; review round 10, F13).
arms.b_overnight: H3-b: entry at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on t+1, timeout 300 s; otherwise no entry (counted). Exit at the first eligible quote at or after 09:30 ET on t+2, under populations.terminal_exits
arms.c_decomposition: H3-c, diagnostic only, not traded, gross, from official prints only: over sessions t+1 .. t+5 of every D event (no entry fill needed), the overnight legs k = 1..4 run from the official close of t+k to the official open of t+k+1, and the intraday legs k = 2..5 run from the official open to the official close of t+k. The partial first-session leg is excluded, so each event has 4 legs of each kind, and together they decompose official close(t+1) to official close(t+5). An event missing any of the 8 legs is excluded from H3-c and counted; no bar or quote substitutes, and no event is averaged over fewer legs.
arms.stops_and_sizing: No stops. Research sizing is 1x equal notional, capacity-capped (cost_model.fix_2_impact_and_capacity).

coverage_rule.scope: All five items, with one set of kept years per stage. It is decided at the freeze from the count-only outputs (exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path), before any outcome, and recorded beside multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze.
coverage_rule.no_fallback: A session or symbol without an accepted official print or an eligible quote stays a counted non-event, no-entry, terminal or excluded trade under its own rule. No bar, quote or other-exchange substitute is ever used.
coverage_rule.year_rule: A calendar year of 2016-2020 is dropped from its stage entirely (every session of that year) if any of these holds, each from the part-1 sample (exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path): (a) its accepted official-close rate is below 90%, where the rate = sampled symbol-sessions with an accepted official close / sampled symbol-sessions with a daily bar and raw close >= $1; (b) its eligible-quote rate is below 80%, where the rate = coverage stamps with an eligible quote / (stamps with an eligible quote + stamps without one + fetch-incomplete stamps), so a fetch-incomplete stamp counts against coverage; (c) its identity-unreached rate (identity_diagnostic) is above 10%; (d) its minute-bar coverage rate is below 90%, where the rate = coverage-selected sampled pairs with daily volume > 0 that have at least one regular-session minute bar / (those pairs with one + those without + those fetch-incomplete) (review round 8, E3). A rate with a zero denominator drops the year. Review round 15, N03: each rate keeps its own cohort, decided by the requests that define membership in it, and a failed request never removes a pair from a cohort; a pair whose membership or outcome is unknown counts against coverage (fail closed): (a) a sampled pair of a batch whose asof = s raw daily request is fetch-incomplete joins the denominator with no accepted close, and a pair with a raw close >= $1 whose auctions request is fetch-incomplete stays in the denominator with no accepted close; (b) a coverage-selected pair of such a raw-incomplete batch counts both its stamps as fetch-incomplete; (c) a pair of a batch whose default-asof raw request is fetch-incomplete counts in the identity-unreached numerator and denominator, and a default-asof member whose asof = s raw request is fetch-incomplete counts as unreached; (d) a coverage-selected pair of a raw-incomplete batch counts as a fetch-incomplete minute pair. Before round 15 any incomplete raw, split, all or auction request dropped the whole sampled batch from every rate. The thresholds are in thresholds. If 2016, the warm-up year, is dropped, events of early 2017 stay unassigned under tercile_rule.minimum until 60 prior events accrue. The thresholds are design choices, not measured values.
coverage_rule.item_rule: If 2020 is dropped, no item is tested: all 5 items score p = 1 at validation and the holdout, permanently, and that is the recorded result of this protocol version. Development years do not condition testing, because development gates nothing (multiple_testing.development_screen) and validation breakpoints use validation sessions only (tercile_rule.breakpoints). If every development year is dropped, development is reported as not computed and every item is underpowered there. (The former condition of at least 2 development years was left over from the removed development gate; review round 7, C13.)
coverage_rule.dropped_year_consequences: (a) Breakpoints: a dropped year's sessions are skipped, and a dropped year's events never enter a trailing window. (b) Segments: each edge of a dropped year is a segment boundary under chronology.boundaries, with censoring and, after it, the embargo. (c) Bootstrap: the stage's kept sessions are concatenated in date order, and the circular block bootstrap wraps over that kept list. Each has a synthetic test with a dropped middle year.
coverage_rule.limitation: The coverage stamps sample the whole $1+ universe, not movers, so mover quote coverage may be lower. Per-stage no-entry, terminal and excluded counts are reported so that this is visible.
coverage_rule.decided_by_code: Nobody applies year_rule, item_rule or any threshold of thresholds by hand (review round 8, R8-9). The count-only code computes each year's three rates and emits the kept or dropped decision per year and the item_rule result. The commit that adds the count-only code records the sha256 of this coverage_rule object, as UTF-8 of json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False), and the code refuses to run if the protocol's coverage_rule hashes differently. The freeze is refused if the frozen coverage_rule hashes differently from the value in the governing count-only run's log entry (review round 7, C9). Review round 15, F04: this object's sha256 is one entry of the count-only output's dependency manifest, not the only binding. The governing output records the study tree that computed it, its runtime lock, the sha256 of both data files it ran against (which the pre-freeze run refuses unless they equal their data-pins.json pins), the parameters' sha256, this object's sha256 and the rate limit, and its first complete 'count_only' run-log line cites it by sha256 and names the same tree, data files, rule and runtime lock. Every run under the frozen protocol refuses (core.runner.check_coverage_decision) unless that line exists and the manifest equals the frozen study_code.tree, data_file_sha256s, parameters, this coverage_rule and pre_freeze_access_path.rate_limit. The count-only run therefore comes after the last change to the study tree and the data files: an output computed by another tree, calendar, fee file or specification never decides the frozen coverage.

fetch_estimate.rule: 40 sessions counted as 40 x 86,400 s (weekends and holidays ignored, so the time is understated); the estimate is the full 2016-2020 screen requests plus, per year, candidate_bound(k) = ceil(20 x (k + 3 sqrt(k) + 3)) candidates times the per-event request count, at the documented rate limit

tercile_rule.breakpoints: For an event decided on session s, the breakpoints are the 1/3 and 2/3 empirical quantiles (numpy 'linear' method) of MAX21 over all D events with a defined MAX21 whose decision session lies in the 252 kept sessions strictly before s. Every D event counts, whether it entered, had no entry or had no fill. Every input is known at the decision. For an event of the validation stage, the window is restricted to validation sessions strictly before s, so no survivorship-limited development or warm-up event sets a validation breakpoint.
tercile_rule.holdout_breakpoints: For a holdout event, the trailing window is the 252 most recent sessions before s that lie outside the gap from 2026-01-02 to N0 - 1. That gap covers #162's reserved holdout, which v3 never reads, and every session from 2026-09-21 to N0 - 1. The window therefore draws only on (a) the sessions ending 2025-12-31 (v1/v2 validation, already exposed), whose screen (daily bars and official prints of sessions s-1 and s with asof = s, enumerated from the same two sources) and per-event MAX21 lookbacks and DV_reg minute bars (asof = t) are all fetched after the freeze under the first granted 'count' entry and sealed before use (review round 8, R8-3; the pre-freeze snapshot is never opened by the count or the read), and (b) earlier holdout sessions. It reads covariates and membership only, never an outcome. A synthetic test computes the breakpoints for the first holdout session from part (a) alone.
tercile_rule.assignment: Low if MAX21 <= the 1/3 breakpoint, high if MAX21 > the 2/3 breakpoint, middle otherwise. A value equal to a breakpoint goes to the lower tercile.
tercile_rule.minimum: If fewer than 60 prior D events with a defined MAX21 lie in the trailing window (an event whose MAX21 is undefined does not count toward the 60, as it does not enter the breakpoints; review round 10, F7), the event is unassigned: it is counted and reported, and it enters neither H1 item. The 2016 warm-up year supplies the first development window. Validation events of early 2020 stay unassigned until 60 prior validation events accrue; they are counted.

holdout.window: 252 sessions (session_calendar) starting at session N0 = the 40th session after the session of the freeze. N0 is fixed by the freeze commit alone. The freeze commit is the first commit reachable from origin/main (first-parent history) in which blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/protocol-core-draft.json has status frozen; the file keeps this path at and after the freeze and is never renamed or moved. The repository squash-merges pull requests, so a commit that exists only on a PR branch is never the freeze commit. Its committer timestamp, converted to America/New_York, is the freeze time. The session of the freeze is the first XNYS session whose scheduled open is at or after the freeze time. D decisions made on session N0 - 1 enter on N0 and belong to the holdout. Development and validation run by committed automation started at the freeze. The commit that adds the validation results file (with its sha256 in the run log) must be reachable from origin/main before 09:30 ET on session N0, measured by the GitHub-recorded time it became reachable (the pull request's merged_at, or the push event for a direct push). If it is not, the holdout of this protocol version is void for every item; a new protocol version is required. There is no deferral. The code measures the time a file or line became reachable from origin/main as the committer time of the first first-parent commit of origin/main that holds it (core/logs.py line_reach, core/holdout.py first_reach). The repository squash-merges pull requests and GitHub sets a squash commit's committer time when it merges, so the committed automation adds every results file and every log and amendment line by pull request (review round 9, M-3). N0 is computed by core/runner.py from the freeze commit and the pinned calendar without its amendments; no command takes N0 or a last session as input, and the last session follows from N0 and the number of extension blocks that committed count results decided (review round 9, M-5). Review round 10, M3: every such time is the committer time of a commit that verifies against the pinned GitHub web-flow key (run_discipline.study_code.rule); GitHub sets and signs it when it merges.
holdout.extension: If any carried item has fewer than its minimum holdout sample after 252 sessions (for H1-D, its smaller group), the holdout is extended in 63-session blocks, at most 2. The window is common to every carried item. A carried item still below its minimum after the second block is labelled underpowered. Each extension decision is made by the committed automation, from one 'count' whose unit is count_unit, never an exit or outcome price.
holdout.count_unit: Integers only, keyed as follows: 'H1-D:high' and 'H1-D:low' (one integer per group, since H1-D is a difference test), 'H1-D-b_lane-low', 'H3-a', 'H3-b' and 'H3-c'. For a tradable cell or an H1-D group, the count is the trades that pass membership and every exclusion, have an entry fill quote inside the entry timeout and filled notional >= $1,000, are not fetch-incomplete, are not excluded by the in-hold split-record rule (populations.suspected_unadjusted_split) and have the tercile the key needs. Their exit is irrelevant, because terminal exits stay in the statistic (populations.terminal_exits). For H3-c, the count is the events with all 8 official legs present. Only presence and exclusion flags, decision-time inputs (MAX21, med20, the entry bar), corporate-action records, the cumulative split factors a(s) of populations.formulas (a ratio of two closes of one session, never a return) and entry-quote presence are evaluated. No mid, spread, return or exit value is computed or emitted. count_unit is used only for the extension decision (review round 8, R8-8): the extension rule applies to the smallest key of each carried item. Every minimum_sample check, at every stage including the holdout read, uses the number of trades (events, for H3-c) that enter the statistic (minimum_sample.rule). A synthetic test asserts that the count output carries exactly these keys with integer values, and that the count path calls no price or return function. Review round 15, F05: the count applies the read's eligibility wherever it is known without an exit price, through the same functions: the record exclusions through E (split record with F = 1, spin-off record; core.trades.record_exclusion), and, when the planned exit session E traded (its raw daily bar exists, so a normal exit books F and the cash term at it), a defined F(entry session, E) and cash term, the latter decided from bar presence and the dividend adjustment factors D(d) = all_c(d) / split_c(d) (ratios of two closes of one session, like a(s); core.costs.cash_defined computes no amount); for H3-c, the spin-off record and each overnight leg's F and cash term. What the count cannot know without the exit stays the read's: an exit-window fetch failure, an undefined F or cash term at a delayed exit session, a record effective after E, and H3-c's check that open x F + cash is positive. count_unit remains an extension input only; every minimum sample uses the read's n.
holdout.why_prospective: No retrospective window free of prior mover outcomes remains: 2021-2025 is v1/v2 dev/val, 2026-01-02 to 2026-09-18 is #162's reserved holdout and is exposed at event level, 2017-2026-08-14 is broad-universe exposed at aggregate level, and 2016 is the warm-up.
holdout.accrual_exposure: The primary holdout statistic of every item uses every holdout trade; nothing is excluded for exposure. Paper exposure is recorded only for symbol-sessions in which a paper order was submitted, logged at order time (symbol, session, order id, strategy) in the collection batch's accrual log before any outcome of that trade exists. A holdout trade is paper-exposed if any session from decision t through its exit is such a symbol-session. A holdout trade whose span from decision t through exit includes a late-collected session (holdout_gate.prospective_collection) is also paper-exposed, because that session's accrual log was not committed in time. The result without paper-exposed trades is reported only as a sensitivity. If the paper-exposed fraction of any carried item's holdout trades exceeds 5%, the holdout is labelled contaminated for that item, and the item cannot then be labelled supported (confirmatory).
holdout.holdout_read: A holdout read is exactly this: computing, from data of sessions N0 onward, any v3-defined outcome (an exit price paired with a v3 entry, a forward, net or leg return of a D event, a terminal booking) or any statistic built from one. Only such a computation inside a granted 'read' entry is permitted. A 'count' entry permits count_unit only. The following are not reads: (1) collection under holdout_gate.prospective_collection, including computing a batch's sha256; (2) live paper decisions and orders of any strategy, including the NautilusTrader paper runs and their decision streams, which are exposure and are logged in the accrual log; (3) dashboards and timers that publish metadata only (counts, liveness, freshness); (4) computing D membership without any outcome, by committed code whose output is logged in the accrual log. A synthetic test classifies one example of each case.
holdout.read_timing: The holdout read is mandatory (review round 7, C6). The committed automation requests the 'read' for every carried item within 15 sessions after the last session of the final block (the terminal-search windows of censored trades end at most 5 sessions after it). No person decides it: the authorization is granted by rule unless an evaluator refusal applies, and then it is recorded 'refused' with that refusal. A read, or a 'count' (review round 8, R8-6), whose completion reports failed with no results file may be retried under a new authorization before the deadline (for a count, before the next scheduled action); a read whose retry chain already sealed a snapshot may be retried after the deadline too, because a sealed read is only ever evaluated (review round 12, F1 of the second review), and it carries 'late-read', from the same study tree and, if one was sealed, the same input snapshot (run_discipline.once). A read that is not completed with a results file by the deadline, is refused, or is void, and a holdout voided for any reason after the gate opened, are numbered deviations, and every carried item is labelled 'not supported (holdout not read)' with the reason (outcome_reporting.rule). No person and no paper result can delay, skip or cancel the read. In code (review round 9, H-1): run.py read (core/holdout.py) writes results/holdout-read.json once. It writes the fixed not-read labels itself, with the reason, when its authorization was refused, a count or its own fetch is void, no final count exists by the deadline, or the deadline has passed.
