Review round 13, F1: 'the holdout is void' means a void deviation that applies by its signed reach time (exposure_registry.update_rule); a void recorded after the gate opened is reported in voids_late and holdout_label and never cancels the read. Review round 13, Codex P2: after a failed count, the block's next count is that count's retry (it names retry_of and meets the retry rule: the same tree, the same sealed snapshot if one exists, before the deadline); a fresh count request is refused, and a completed count's retries seal into and read from the first attempt's snapshot directory (core.holdout.sealed_refs). Review round 11, F1: whether the holdout is read never depends on its outcome. (1) Once any read has a committed 'read_fetch' line (its sealed snapshot holds the exit quotes), the only allowed result is that read's evaluation over that snapshot, whatever the time; a read whose fetch line or evaluation came at or after the deadline carries the qualifier 'late-read' and its labels stand, and a count or holdout void recorded after the seal is reported in void_after_seal, never turned into the not-read label. (2) A granted read whose authorization reached origin/main before the deadline is always carried out, a fetch after the deadline included. (3) The not-read labels are written for a granted read that sealed nothing only when its authorization reached origin/main at or after the deadline, no final count exists, a count is void or the holdout is void. (4) A refused read authorization is a failed attempt, not a decision that can be held back: run.py read spends it only after the deadline has passed by a signed commit on origin/main, only if no read sealed a snapshot, only if it is the latest 'read' authorization and only if no granted 'read' is open; it is committed before it is spent, so the spend is logged and pre-committed. Limitation: code cannot compel a person to request the read; if no read authorization reaches origin/main before the deadline, the not-read label follows, which never supports a claim. Review round 11, F2: every holdout due time is judged by the signed time the action's authorization reached origin/main: a collect needs it after the close of the batch's last session, a count after the close of the window's last session, and a read's fetch after the close of the last terminal-search session. Every holdout action also refuses an access-log or holdout run-log record whose time is later than the signed time of the commit that first held it on origin/main (a clock set forward). Review round 12, Codex P2: a count's or read's '_fetch' line pins the ordered base snapshots (every sealed collection batch and count, by directory and sha256) and the collection batches it used, and the evaluation step, a retry included, reads exactly those, so a collection batch completed after the seal (for example after a failed evaluation) can change neither the plan nor any row of the evaluation.

labels.development: disjoint from v1/v2; exposed at aggregate level through broad-universe development; screening only; survivorship-limited (names delisted in 2016-2019 without a retained corporate action cannot be discovered); descriptive only, so it gates nothing (multiple_testing.development_screen)
labels.validation: disjoint from v1/v2; exposed at aggregate level through broad-universe development and the S2 headline the author read; screening only, never confirmatory; the 2020 COVID regime is never dropped; not labelled survivorship-limited on the delisting measure: the broad-universe survivorship measure (known_inactive_or_supplement_last_bar_year_histogram in blueprints/us-equities/broad-universe/receipt.json, from the same asset-master and corporate-action sources as universe_and_identity.enumeration) counts 563 names whose last bar falls in 2020, inside the 2021-2025 range of 512-756, against 371 in 2019 and 25-167 in 2016-2018. That is a measured count on entitled sources, not proof of completeness, and it was measured under broad-universe's default-asof requests, so it does not cover what asof = s screening misses. The identity diagnostic decides that part (exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path.identity_diagnostic): if 2020's identity-unreached rate exceeds 2% (coverage_rule.thresholds.identity_limited_validation_rate; the count-only code emits the decision, review round 8, R8-9), every validation result is labelled identity-limited, with the rate stated. Validation uses no development data: its tercile breakpoints come from validation sessions only (tercile_rule.breakpoints), and no development output is an input (multiple_testing.development_screen)
labels.holdout: prospective; untouched only if the validation results commit was reachable from origin/main before 09:30 ET on N0, no holdout read preceded a committed granted access-log entry, every holdout count and read ran from the frozen study_code tree or a passing transport deviation of it (run_discipline.study_code, run_discipline.transport_deviations), every collection batch has its committed accrual log, and no carried item's paper-exposed fraction exceeds 5% In code (review round 11, C8): results/holdout-read.json carries holdout_label, 'untouched' or the list of the failed conditions, computed from the committed state (core.holdout.holdout_label).

chronology.boundaries: Segments are assigned by entry session (for H3-c, by session t+1). A D decision whose entry session (for H3-c, session t+1) lies in no segment, such as a decision on 2020-12-31 (entry 2021-01-04) or on the last kept session before a dropped year, is dropped and counted per stage. A trade whose planned exit falls after its segment's last session is censored: it exits at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on that last session, searching past the segment end if needed (populations.terminal_exits.segment_end), is flagged, stays in its segment's statistics and is reported as a count. H3-b makes no entry on a segment's last session (counted). An H3-c event whose legs cross the segment end is excluded from H3-c and counted. Embargo: every item (H1-D, H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a, H3-b, H3-c) gives up the first 6 sessions of validation, and the first 6 kept sessions after a dropped year, as entry sessions. This keeps the censored and delayed trades of the earlier segment, whose exit search runs up to 5 sessions past its last session, clear of later entries. Review round 15, F10: H3-a is embargoed too; its planned exit is on its entry session, but an exit with no eligible quote searches through E+5 (populations.terminal_exits), so its permitted horizon reaches 6 sessions. There is no embargo at N0: the holdout follows years after validation, no v3 trade is open in the sessions before N0 (those sessions are lookback inputs only), and D decisions on N0 - 1 enter on N0. A synthetic test covers the embargo after development, the embargo after a dropped year, and a 5-session trade entered on N0 that is kept.

labels.passes_stage: The item passes its stage rule. The pass has a stage-specific name: 'development pass' at development (descriptive only; it gates nothing, multiple_testing.development_screen), 'screened' at validation (Holm in the 5-item family, the minimum sample and, for a tradable cell, the robustness means), and 'supported (confirmatory)' at the holdout (the same rule, and for H3-c the validation sign of multiple_testing.no_direction_lock). Only the holdout label is a claim.
labels.not_supported_mde_excluded: The stage has at least its minimum sample, the item does not pass, and the one-sided bootstrap-percentile confidence bound (from the same B draws, numpy 'linear' quantile) at Bonferroni level a = 0.05/5 = 0.01 excludes an effect of the preregistered MDE for the realized n (minimum_detectable_effect). For the alternative 'less than 0' (H1-D), the bound is the a-quantile of the bootstrap statistics, and the MDE is excluded when that bound is greater than -MDE. For the alternative 'greater than 0' (every tradable cell), the bound is the (1 - a)-quantile, and the MDE is excluded when it is less than +MDE. H3-c is two-sided at every stage: it uses a = 0.05/10 and requires both conditions, the lower bound (the a-quantile) greater than -MDE and the upper bound (the (1 - a)-quantile) less than +MDE. The fixed Bonferroni level is used because Holm's step-down level is not defined for items after the first retained hypothesis. Review round 15, F06: the bounds are statistics.p_value's conservative bounds (a draw with no statistic cannot support an exclusion), and the label needs statistics.inference_validity.
labels.underpowered: The stage is below its minimum sample, or the stage is void (populations.fetch_failures), or the item's bootstrap fails statistics.inference_validity (review round 15, F06), or the item neither passes nor excludes the MDE.

outcome_reporting.hypothesis_verdict: Each hypothesis gets exactly one verdict per stage, from its primary contrast alone: H1-D for H1 and H3-c for H3 (item_set: the direct test of H1, and the direct test of H3's 'versus'). Review round 15, F07: the tradable cells answer whether a leg is profitable after costs, not whether the hypothesis holds, so they are reported separately (outcome_reporting.profitability) and never decide a verdict; before round 15 any passing item of a hypothesis, a cell included, promoted it to a pass verdict, so H3 could be 'screened' on H3-a alone. By the first rule that applies: (1) Pass: the primary contrast has the stage's pass name ('development pass', 'screened' or 'supported (confirmatory)'); the verdict takes it with the contrast's qualifiers. (2) Not supported: the primary contrast is labelled not_supported_mde_excluded; and at the holdout, 'not supported (holdout not read)' if the contrast has that label. (3) Inconclusive: every other case, including an underpowered contrast and one labelled 'screened (contaminated holdout)'. A verdict is computed at development (descriptive), at validation (the screening verdict) and, for a hypothesis whose primary contrast was carried, at the holdout (the confirmatory verdict); a hypothesis whose primary contrast was not carried gets no holdout verdict (core/stats.py hypothesis_verdict).
outcome_reporting.profitability: Review round 15, F07: the three tradable cells (H1-D-b_lane-low for H1; H3-a and H3-b for H3) are reported per stage beside the verdicts, each with its hypothesis, its label, whether it passed the stage (at validation and the holdout that includes the robustness means) and its qualifiers (core/stats.py profitability). A passing cell is evidence that the leg was tradable after costs in that stage; it is never a verdict on H1 or H3. At the holdout only carried cells are reported. The holdout gate still opens for every validated item, cells included (holdout_gate.opens_only_for).
outcome_reporting.validation_reporting: Every item receives its validation p and enters the validation Holm run, whatever its development result. Development is survivorship-limited, so it nominates nothing and never removes an item from validation or the holdout. An item scores p = 1 at validation only when it is not tested (coverage_rule) or validation is void (populations.fetch_failures, run_discipline.deviations). The H1 high and middle b_lane cells are reported descriptively at every stage, with no p-value.
outcome_reporting.qualifiers: Contamination, lineage and deviation status are qualifiers attached to a label, never labels of their own. A holdout item that meets the pass rule while its holdout is contaminated is labelled 'screened (contaminated holdout)', never 'supported (confirmatory)'. An item labelled 'supported (confirmatory)' that is not lineage-confirmed (multiple_testing.lineage_sensitivity) carries 'lineage-unconfirmed'. A stage whose data were fetched or collected under a transport deviation (run_discipline.transport_deviations) carries 'transport-deviation'.
outcome_reporting.rule: Only these three labels are used, with the qualifiers above, plus one fixed label: a carried item whose holdout is not read by the deadline, is refused or is void is labelled 'not supported (holdout not read)' with the reason and no excluded size (chronology.holdout.read_timing). No run from a deviated study tree (other than a passing transport deviation) is possible: core.guards.check_study_tree refuses it, so no such result exists (review round 11, C14). A miss is never reported as 'falsified' or as proof of no effect, and 'not supported' otherwise always states the size it excludes. A result in the direction opposite to a one-sided alternative, or for H3-c at the holdout opposite to the validation sign, is reported descriptively with its estimate and interval and supports no claim. In code (review round 11, C12): every computed item carries opposite_direction (true for an estimate opposite a one-sided alternative, or for H3-c at the holdout opposite the validation sign) with its estimate and interval_95. Such an item never passes: for a one-sided item this is enforced by rule in core.stats.item_label (opposite), not only by the size of its bootstrap p (review round 12, F9), and for H3-c at the holdout by the sign check. Its label is unchanged and may be 'not_supported_mde_excluded', because its interval then excludes the alternative's size; the flag states that the estimate supports no claim of an effect in the opposite direction.

multiple_testing.family: One family of m = 5 items (item_set): H1-D, H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a, H3-b, H3-c. H6 and the deferred H2, H4 and H5 are not in it.
multiple_testing.item_id_rule: item_ids is the complete list, in bytewise ASCII order. That order is used for stream spawning, for the final tie-break and for the validation results file.
multiple_testing.procedure: Holm step-down at family-wise alpha 0.05, applied separately at validation and at the holdout, over these 5 items only. An item not carried to a stage, or not tested for lack of data, scores p = 1 there. The validation results file contains all 5 validation p-values keyed by item_ids (1 only for items not tested); the evaluator refuses an incomplete file. In code (review round 10, F5): core.gate.validation_complete requires items and labels keyed by exactly the 5 item_ids, each with a numeric p_stage in [0, 1], and the evaluator refuses a 'count' or 'read' otherwise.
multiple_testing.no_direction_lock: H3-c's p is two-sided at every stage, with the two-sided p of statistics.p_value in its Holm slot, and no development output sets its direction. The full draft and the first core draft locked H3-c after development to the sign of its development estimate. That lock is removed (review round 6): development is survivorship-limited, and a lock set by a survivorship-biased estimate could stop H3-c from ever validating or reaching the holdout. At the holdout, a confirmatory pass of H3-c also needs the holdout estimate to have the sign of the governing validation estimate (review round 7, C7). Validation is the governing screen and is not survivorship-limited on the delisting measure, and H3-c is carried only if it validated, so that estimate is nonzero. A significant holdout estimate of the other sign is reported descriptively with its estimate and interval and supports no claim. A synthetic test asserts that validation and holdout p-values do not change when every development output is altered, and that a significant holdout H3-c opposite to the validation sign does not pass.
multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze: At the freeze, H1 and H3 are each recorded as either 'data in hand, tested' or 'not tested, p = 1 at every stage, permanently', by coverage_rule. Data from a new source, or a new historical range acquired after the freeze, can support only a new protocol version with its own family (v3.1+), never this family's Holm run. The prospective Alpaca SIP data collected under holdout_gate.prospective_collection are not new data in this sense.
multiple_testing.development_screen: Unadjusted p <= 0.05 with the minimum sample: one-sided in the stated direction for H1-D, H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a and H3-b, and two-sided for H3-c. Development is descriptive: its pass ('development pass') is reported for every item and gates nothing. Every item goes to validation (outcome_reporting.validation_reporting). No development output (an estimate, a sign, a pass or an event's tercile breakpoint) is an input to validation, the holdout gate or any holdout statistic, because 2017-2019 is survivorship-limited (chronology.labels.development).
multiple_testing.lineage_sensitivity: The mover question has already tried 1,012 rule-exits (v1 768, v2 244) and broad-universe-mover-v1's 60 predeclared signal variants on overlapping or other windows. Every validation and holdout p is also reported against Bonferroni 0.05 / (1012 + 60 + 5) = 4.64e-5. The archived 35-item draft computed nothing and is not counted. broad-universe's controls and descriptive lane have no pass rule and are not counted, which is a stated limitation. Each p is reported beside the normal-tail p of statistics.normal_tail_p. With B = 100,000, a bootstrap p at 4.64e-5 means at most 3 null-side draws, so the bootstrap p alone cannot resolve this level. An item is lineage-confirmed only if both its bootstrap p and its normal-tail p are at or below 4.64e-5.
multiple_testing.tie_breaks: Where items tie on a p (for example at the floor 1 / (B + 1)) in Holm ordering or in reporting, ties are broken by the normal-tail p, then by item id in bytewise ASCII order. A tie's order never changes a Holm-adjusted p (the step-down's running maximum gives tied items the same adjusted p), so the rule is observable only in the order itself: the validation and holdout results carry holm_order, the step-down order core.stats.holm_order computes and core.stats.holm uses (review round 12, F5).
multiple_testing.tests_not_in_family: BH (q = 0.10) diagnostics across year, price-tier and tercile splits are reported but can never open the holdout. Each split's diagnostic p is the normal approximation of its trade-level mean in the item's direction, with a standard error clustered by entry session (review round 12, Codex P2: trades that share a session are not independent): se^2 = G / (G - 1) x the sum over the split's G sessions of (the session's summed (x - mean) / n)^2, which equals sd / sqrt(n) when each session holds one trade; fewer than 2 sessions give p = 1. BH runs over one tradable cell's splits, and each split reports its n and its number of sessions.

minimum_sample.H3-c: the tradable_cell minima, counted as events with all 8 legs
minimum_sample.rule: A stage below its minimum reports the item as underpowered; it cannot pass that stage. Review round 8, R8-8: n is the number of trades (for H3-c, events) that enter the item's statistic at that stage, after every exclusion (an undefined F among them), at development, validation and the holdout read alike; for H1-D, each group (high and low) must reach the per-group minimum. count_unit counts only for the holdout extension decision.

minimum_detectable_effect.formula: MDE = (z_alpha + z(0.80)) x sigma x sqrt(DEFF) x sqrt(1/n) for one cell or H3-c. For H1-D, sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2) replaces sqrt(1/n), with n1 and n2 the realized high and low group sizes. z_alpha = z(1 - 0.05/5) = 2.326 for the one-sided tests (H1-D and the three tradable cells), and z(1 - 0.05/10) = 2.576 for H3-c, which is two-sided at every stage. The MDE is computed from the planning sigma below and the realized n (the n of minimum_sample.rule, review round 8, R8-8), and it is never re-estimated from outcomes.

sigma_by_item.rule: Every item has an entry: [planning sigma, MDE form]. 'difference' uses sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2), 'cell' uses sqrt(1/n), and 'paired' is a one-sample paired statistic with sqrt(1/n).

minimum_detectable_effect.sigma_provenance: 0.25 (the same-session close arm, H3-a) is (P95 - P5) / 3.29 from #162 v1 development aggregates for the 07:00|G0.20|V1000000 X1 exit (P5 -42.1%, P95 +39.5%), a normal approximation that understates fat tails. Those rule-exits entered at 07:00 ET in the pre-market, so the spread for 09:35 entries is not measured. The other values are assumptions with no measured source: 0.35 for the 5-session b_lane arm, 0.15 for one 15:55-to-09:30 overnight leg (H3-b), and 0.10 for the difference of two 4-leg means of log returns (H3-c). DEFF 1.5 for session clustering is also an assumption.
minimum_detectable_effect.units: Review round 15, F14: the tables are 100 x the MDE. For H1-D and the tradable cells that is a percent of the (net) return; for H3-c it is log points, 100 x the difference of two mean log returns, not a percent return (the former key mde_percent_H3-c named it wrongly). Every item result states its units and reports its occupied entry sessions (for H1-D per group), the clusters the session bootstrap resamples.
minimum_detectable_effect.reading: Only large effects can pass or be excluded. The literature's MAX effect (about 1% a month) is far below these MDEs, so a miss on H1-D will most likely be labelled underpowered. v3 is informative only about large mover-specific effects.

base_table.note: The v1 table, unchanged from the PR branch commit 92062e8 to main at aa6fc79. D7 records that it reproduces byte for byte under the stamp-window check. v3 refuses a table with another hash.

lookup.cell_key: time_bucket|price_tier|dv_tier, per side, from that side's fill: the time bucket of the fill timestamp, the price tier of the fill price, and the dv tier of the session's cumulative dollar volume at the fill timestamp: the summed vwap x volume of the session's 1-minute bars from 04:00 ET that are complete by the fill, i.e. that start at or before the fill time minus 60 s (rules.py Bars.cum_dv arithmetic over those bars only; review round 15, F02: counting every bar that starts before the fill, as rules.py's cum_dv(ts) does, counted the volume of the minute still trading at the fill, which could move the fill into a more liquid, cheaper tier).
lookup.buckets: time buckets [04:00, 08:00), [08:00, 09:30), [09:30, 10:00), [10:00, 16:01) ET; price tiers [0, 2), [2, 5), [5, 20), [20, inf) dollars; dv tiers [0, 1M), [1M, 5M), [5M, inf). Every interval is half-open, so a boundary value goes to the upper tier ($5.00 is in $5-20), as the pinned copies of rules.py time_bucket, price_tier (numpy searchsorted side='right') and dv_tier do (review round 8, R8-12).

fix_1_monotone_dollar_volume.rule: For each time x price bucket: hs'(>= $5M) = hs(>= $5M); hs'($1-5M) = max(hs($1-5M), hs'(>= $5M)); hs'(< $1M) = max(hs(< $1M), hs'($1-5M)). A less liquid tier is never cheaper than a more liquid one.
fix_1_monotone_dollar_volume.finding: #162 review item costs-F1: cells under $1M dollar volume fell back to a time x price pool costing about half the $1-5M cell

fix_2_impact_and_capacity.notional: Filled notional = min($20,000; 1% of med20; 10% of the entry bar's dollar volume, vwap x volume), with med20 and the entry bar as populations.formulas defines them. The excess is not filled. A trade with filled notional under $1,000, or one that cannot be sized, is a no-fill and is counted.
fix_2_impact_and_capacity.impact: Impact per side (as a return) = c x sigma_d x sqrt(q), where q = filled notional / med20 and sigma_d is from populations.formulas, both known at the decision. The primary value is c = 1.0, with sensitivities at c = 0.5 and 2.0. The square-root form and the c grid are design choices bracketing the unknown.

cost_model.per_side: Cost per side = 1.25 x max(hs'(cell), h_fill) + impact, where h_fill = (ask - bid) / (ask + bid) is the realized half-spread of the fill quote as a fraction of the mid. The realized floor measures each fill's own period and quote, so the full draft's 2017-2019 re-measure of the table is not needed. The table-only cost (1.25 x hs'(cell) + impact, v1's convention) is a sensitivity. The stress cost is 2 x 1.25 x max(hs'(cell), h_fill) + impact at c = 2.0. Terminal exits follow populations.terminal_exits.booking.
cost_model.fees: Fees come from data/fees-v3.json, pinned by sha256 at the freeze (run_discipline.data_files). It carries the SEC Section 31 and FINRA TAF rows in force from 2017-01-01 through the freeze, each with its primary source and quote; every TAF row and TAF amendment line carries its max_usd_per_trade cap, and the fee is min(TAF usd_per_share x shares, cap) plus the SEC usd_per_million x sell value / 1e6, unrounded (review round 8, R8-12). Review round 15, N01: the file is read in its committed schema (schema_version 1; sec_section31.rows with usd_per_million and finra_taf_covered_equity.rows with usd_per_share and max_usd_per_trade, each table in its stated unit; a null 'to' on a row is its open end), and core.costs.Fees refuses another schema or unit; a synthetic test loads the committed file and finds a governing row for every development and validation sale. Rates announced after the freeze are appended only as lines of data/fees-v3-amendments.jsonl in run_discipline.amendment_format, from primary sources, committed and logged in the access log (purpose 'amend') before the first holdout count or read that uses their dates; the evaluator refuses a line that reached origin/main after that count or read (review round 8, R8-10). They concern dates on or after the freeze session and never change an earlier line. #162 fees.json at aa6fc79 is not used. Alpaca commission is 0. Review round 15, fee-date item: a sale's SEC row is the one in force on its charge (settlement) date and its TAF row the one in force on its trade date, under the settlement cycle in force on the trade date (cost_model.fee_charge_dates). A synthetic test looks up a 2017 and a 2019 sale and a post-freeze amended rate, and tests/test_costs.py ChargeDates crosses the SEC boundaries on settlement dates and the TAF boundaries on trade dates. In code (review round 10, F2): run.py authorize --purpose amend appends the 'amend' authorization; once it is on origin/main, run.py amend --authorization ID --file calendar|fees --line N appends its completion, which cites the file, the line index, the line's sha256 and its primary source. core.runner.context refuses every other run while an amendment line has no such record, or while the record reached origin/main at or after the line's deadline (the first holdout count or read that uses its dates). Review round 13, Codex P2: a read's trades exit, and pay sale fees, through the end of the last terminal-search window, 5 sessions after the window's last session, so every holdout read line records fee_span = [N0, last + 5 sessions] and a fee line's first use is the first count or read whose fee_span (or, for a count, its sessions) overlaps its dates (core.logs.fee_first_use); a line for those dates appended after a failed read is refused on the retry. Review round 14, F2: the base file's rows of one kind never overlap, and each runs from <= to; a base that breaks this is refused when the fees are loaded, never inside a read. An amendment line supersedes, for the dates it covers, every earlier row of its kind (the base's open-ended last row included): the latest appended line that covers a date governs, and a base row governs a date no amendment line covers. No line is edited; supersession is by precedence. A count (its sessions) and a read (its fee_span) each refuse, before they fetch or log anything, while a session of their span has no governing SEC Section 31 or FINRA TAF row (core.holdout.require_fee_coverage), so the missing line can still be appended and logged; a fee failure can therefore no longer first appear inside a read's evaluation and lock out every corrective line. A count's or read's '_fetch' line is a use too (its sessions, and a read's fee_span), so no fee line for those dates can be added between the sealed fetch and the evaluation.

fee_charge_dates.convention: Review round 15, fee-date item. The simulated sale is a regular-way sale of an exchange-listed equity executed on an exchange and cleared and settled through NSCC. Its SEC Section 31 row is the one in force on its charge date, which for such a sale is its settlement date: 17 CFR 240.31(a)(3)(i) makes the settlement date the charge date of a covered sale that a covered SRO reports from data it receives from a designated clearing agency (quoted in data/fees-v3.json sec_section31.date_basis_source), and Release 34-49928 applies it to every covered sale a covered exchange reports to NSCC. Its FINRA TAF row is the one in force on its trade date (data/fees-v3.json finra_taf_covered_equity.date_basis: FINRA applies its rates to transactions). So a SEC row's from and to, and a SEC amendment line's, are charge dates, and a TAF row's and a TAF line's are trade dates (run_discipline.amendment_format).
fee_charge_dates.settlement_cycle: The cycle in force on the trade session: T+3 before 2017-09-05, T+2 from 2017-09-05 (SEC statement 2017-163), T+1 from 2024-05-28 (SEC press release 2023-29, the compliance date). Sales on 2017-09-01 (T+3) and 2017-09-05 (T+2) both settle on 2017-09-07, and sales on 2024-05-24 (T+2) and 2024-05-28 (T+1) both settle on 2024-05-29. Early development (2017-01-03 through 2017-09-01) therefore settles T+3.
fee_charge_dates.settlement_days: The settlement date is the k-th settlement day after the trade session (k from settlement_cycle). A settlement day is a session of the session calendar the run uses (the amended calendar) that is not a Federal Reserve holiday on which the exchange opens: Columbus Day (the second Monday of October) and Veterans Day (November 11; the Monday after when it falls on a Sunday; none when it falls on a Saturday, when the Federal Reserve Banks open on the Friday). FINRA Rule 11320(e): a contract due on a day other than a business day matures on the next business day. Limitations: the Federal Reserve observance rule is encoded as stated, not retrieved from an SEC or FINRA document in this round, and a session an amendment removes counts as no settlement day. No SEC row of data/fees-v3.json starts within four sessions after such a bank-only holiday, so the rule changes the selection of no pinned row (tests/test_costs.py ChargeDates); it matters only for a later amendment line dated near one.
fee_charge_dates.not_modelled: A sale executed otherwise than on an exchange (for example internalized by an off-exchange market maker and reported to a FINRA trade reporting facility) has its trade date as its charge date (17 CFR 240.31(a)(3)(iv); Release 34-49928: the association reports such sales from its trade reporting systems), so its SEC row differs from this convention's only for sales in the last one to three sessions before a SEC rate change, by the rate difference times the sale value. The study does not model a venue: it freezes the exchange and NSCC convention, which the Commission describes as the charge date of most covered sales in equity securities. Broker rounding of the pass-through stays unmodelled (data/fees-v3.json not_modelled).

cost_model.break_even: The cost multiple at which each tradable cell's mean net return reaches 0 is reported: k scales both per-side costs (k x c_in, k x c_out; fees and terminal-zero trades unchanged) and is found by bisection on [0, 64] to 1e-6; none if the mean is not positive at k = 0, 64 if it is still positive there.

statistics.estimator: The trade-level mean net return (for H3-c, the event-level mean leg difference). The median is also reported for every item, and the three robustness statistics for the tradable cells, where they are part of the pass rule (review round 11, C13: they are not computed for H1-D or H3-c).
statistics.bootstrap: A circular session block bootstrap, B = 100,000, over the stage's kept sessions concatenated in date order (sessions keyed by entry session; for H3-c, by t+1). Block length is 10 sessions for every item (review round 15, F10: H3-a's 5 was chosen for a same-session hold, but its exit search runs through E+5, so its trades can span 6 sessions; the 10 sessions the other items use cover each item's longest permitted hold, b_lane's 5 sessions plus its E+5 search, and are kept uniform rather than tuned per item). H1-D resamples sessions jointly for both groups. The generator is numpy.random.Generator(PCG64), seeded per stage (stage_index 0 development, 1 validation, 2 holdout). Each stage uses numpy.random.SeedSequence(entropy = the first 8 bytes of sha256(frozen protocol id) read big-endian, spawn_key = (stage_index,)).spawn(5), and child i drives item_ids[i] through numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(child)). Each draw's block starts come from Generator.integers(0, n, size=(rows, ceil(n / L))) in consecutive chunks of 10,000 rows; start i contributes sessions i .. i+L-1 (mod n), and the concatenation is cut to the n kept sessions (core/stats.py).
statistics.p_value: One-sided p = (1 + #{b : stat_b on the null side of 0}) / (B + 1), where the null side is closed: stat_b <= 0 for the alternative 'greater than 0' and stat_b >= 0 for 'less than 0'. A draw in which an H1-D group or a cell has no trade has no statistic and counts as a null-side draw, for either side (review round 8, R8-11). Two-sided p = min(1, 2 x the smaller one-sided p). The normal-tail sd and the descriptive interval_95 use the draws that have a statistic. Review round 15, F06: the MDE-exclusion bounds of outcome_reporting use all B draws, a draw with no statistic placed beyond every defined draw on the side that cannot support an exclusion (+inf for an upper bound, -inf for a lower bound; core.stats.conservative_bound), as the p-value places it on the null side.
statistics.normal_tail_p: z = estimate / sd(the B bootstrap statistics, ddof = 1). For the alternative 'greater than 0', p_N = 1 - Phi(z); for 'less than 0', p_N = Phi(z); two-sided (H3-c) p_N = min(1, 2 x min(Phi(z), 1 - Phi(z))). Phi is the standard normal CDF, and p_N = 1 if the sd is 0. It is used only for lineage confirmation and tie-breaks.
statistics.inference_validity: Review round 15, F06: an item's bootstrap supports a label only if (1) occupied-cluster eligibility holds: the share of draws with no statistic (a draw in which the item, or an H1-D group, has no trade) is at most the item's tail level, 0.05 / 5 for a one-sided item and 0.05 / 10 for H3-c; with blocks of L sessions this needs the trades to span several blocks (G occupied sessions more than L apart leave about exp(-1)^G of the draws empty, so about 5 such sessions one-sided and 6 two-sided); and (2) the inference is not degenerate: at least two draws have a statistic and they are not all equal. Otherwise the item can neither pass nor be labelled not_supported_mde_excluded, whatever its p and its bounds, and it is 'underpowered' (core.stats.inference_check, item_label's inference_ok). Every item result reports its occupied entry sessions (per group for H1-D) and the undefined-draw share. At e7529b47 H1-D could meet its 100-per-group minimum inside one entry session: with coinciding group means the defined draws were all 0, the bounds dropped the undefined draws, and the item was labelled not_supported_mde_excluded on a zero-width interval.
statistics.robustness_required_for_a_pass: A tradable cell's validation and holdout passes also need all three of these to be > 0, each computed from that stage's trades of that cell. (1) The winsorised mean: the trade-level mean after clipping each trade net return to [q01, q99], the numpy.quantile 'linear' 0.01 and 0.99 quantiles of those returns (1% in each tail). (2) The mean without the top 5 sessions: sum trade net returns by entry session, drop the 5 entry sessions with the largest sums (a tie is broken by dropping the earlier session first), and take the trade-level mean of the remaining trades. (3) The mean of per-session means: the equal-weighted mean, over entry sessions, of each session's trade-level mean. A synthetic test fixes each on a small table.
sensitivities: two-way (session, symbol) clustering: the trade-level mean with a Cameron-Gelbach-Miller two-way cluster-robust standard error, V = V_session + V_symbol - V_session x symbol, floored at the larger one-way V
validation restricted to symbol-sessions that were not a broad-universe lane decision (exposure_registry.consequence)
table-only cost, and the stress cost
every terminal-zero trade rebooked at the last eligible bid of its hold (populations.terminal_exits)
trades whose hold spans a session flagged by the ratio rule of populations.suspected_unadjusted_split removed
statistics.sensitivities_per_item: Review round 10, F3: each sensitivity is the item's own statistic on the named subset or variant: the high-minus-low difference of trade-level means for H1-D, the mean leg difference for H3-c and the trade-level mean for a tradable cell (core/evaluate.py sensitivities). Every item reports the least-exposed slice (exposure_registry.consequence), beside each validation result, with its size, the holdout without paper-exposed trades and two-way clustering (for H1-D, of the difference, from each trade's influence on it). H1-D and the tradable cells also report the table-only and stress costs, the impact-constant sensitivities, the terminal-zero rebooking, the ratio-rule removal and the censored removal. H3-c has no cost, no terminal booking and no censored leg (an event whose legs cross a segment end is excluded), so those do not apply to it.

holdout_gate.opens_only_for: Items that passed validation: Holm-adjusted validation p <= 0.05 in the 5-item family, the minimum validation sample (for H1-D, in each group) and, for a tradable cell (H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a, H3-b), the three robustness statistics. There is no cap: every validated item is carried. A synthetic gate test carries three validated tradable cells including H3-a, and refuses one that fails a robustness statistic. Review round 12, F1: the carried items are rechecked when the count and the read run, not only at authorization: the authorization's requested_items must equal the validated items of the governing validation file (order-insensitive), or the action is refused, so a committed record listing a subset cannot leave a validated item out of the read or out of the not-read label. An action also refuses to run under an authorization record that lacks any access_log.fields.authorization field. Review round 14, Codex P1: the validation results file is bound by its sha256. The authorization record carries the validation_results_sha256 it was evaluated on, and every count and read (both steps, and the not-read label) refuses unless the working validation file's sha256 equals that value and the governing run-log line's results_sha256; the read's H3-c sign comes from those bound bytes (core.holdout.require_validated_carried). A local edit of the validation file after the gate opened, such as the H3-c estimate's sign, is refused, never read.
holdout_gate.no_pass: If nothing validates, the holdout is never labelled or read, and that is the result. In code (review round 10, F8): a 'read' authorization refused because nothing validated makes run.py read write results/holdout-read.json with no label and no verdict, only a record that nothing validated (no_holdout).
holdout_gate.prospective_collection: The frozen collector collects forward from the session of the freeze: its plan (sessions, symbols, asof, the rename re-fetch) is core/plan.py and its records core/store.py, and only the transport is under study/fetch/ (review round 8, R8-1). Each batch holds screen data only, for the whole enumerated list (universe_and_identity.enumeration, refreshed per batch): the daily bars (raw, split and all) and official prints of sessions s-1 and s for each collected session s, with asof = s, plus corporate-action records. Batches are sealed into a private snapshot whose sha256 is committed per batch with its accrual log. No quote and no minute bar is collected, and nothing selects symbols by membership. Everything else a holdout event needs (lookbacks, minute bars, entry, exit and terminal-search quotes, hold-period prints) is fetched only under a granted 'count' or 'read' entry, by the frozen fetch code with the event's asof = t (universe_and_identity.asof), and sealed before use. Sessions from the freeze to N0 - 1 serve only as lookback inputs. No outcome is computed from any batch before a granted 'read' entry. Timeliness is judged per session (review round 11, C3): session s is timely only if the batch holding it, with its accrual log, is reachable from origin/main before 09:30 ET of the session after s, so a multi-session batch leaves every session but its last late unless it reached main within that session (core.plan.late_collected). A session with no timely batch is collected by the next batch, flagged late-collected and counted; it stays in the holdout (collection is not a read), and chronology.holdout.accrual_exposure treats trades that span it as paper-exposed. Because the asof mapping of a renamed symbol may become available only after the rename day, each batch also re-fetches once, logged, the rows of sessions s-1 and s under the new symbol with asof = s for every name_change record effective (process_date) on a session s of the previous batch, and those rows join session s's screen (counted per batch; review round 7, F9). In code (review round 9, H-1 and M-6): each batch is one run of run.py collect under its own committed granted 'collect' authorization. It collects every session from the session after the previous complete batch (the freeze session for the first) through a closed session, refreshes the enumeration into its own snapshot (sealed as <root>/collect-<authorization id>), and its completion record carries the batch's accrual log. A count or read reads every sealed batch through core/holdout_store.py, which merges the screen per (symbol, session): the row of session s for symbol X comes from the latest batch whose asof = s request names X, and the rename re-fetch rows join it. A count or read is refused while any session from N0 - 1 through the window's last session is in no batch. A symbol-session that no batch holds, because its symbol entered the enumeration later, is fetched by the count or read with asof = s and sealed in its snapshot.

access_log.mode: append-only JSON lines of two record kinds. An 'authorization' record is committed and pushed before the action it authorizes and carries no value that exists only after that action. A 'completion' record is appended, committed and pushed after the action ends (complete, failed or partial), before any later authorization; it never edits its authorization.

authorization: code_revision (the commit run at, provenance only)
retry_of (the failed read's authorization_id, or null)
completion: results_sha256 (null if no results file was written)

purposes.collect: a collection batch; its completion has rows_read 0 and lists that batch's accrual exposure
purposes.amend: one calendar or fee amendment line, with its primary source
purposes.count: at the end of the 252 sessions and of each extension block: count_unit per carried item, used only for the extension decision; it may fetch the entry quotes, lookbacks, minute bars and prints the count needs, under run_discipline.fetch
purposes.read: the single mandatory outcome read for carried items (chronology.holdout.read_timing)

access_log.rule: Any holdout read without a preceding committed granted entry of the matching purpose voids the holdout for every item. Refusals are logged too, as authorization records with decision 'refused' and no completion. A granted authorization without its completion blocks every later authorization, and a granted 'read' authorization counts as the one holdout read unless its completion reports failed with no results file, in which case only a retry under chronology.holdout.read_timing may follow. The same retry rule applies to a 'count' whose completion reports failed with no results file (review round 8, R8-6). The synthetic suite tests the 'count' path, including a test that it computes no exit price, and the log for a complete, a failed and a partial read, each an authorization followed by its completion, and a failed count followed by its permitted retry (core/gate.py, tests/test_gate.py). In code (review round 9, H-1 and F2): run.py authorize computes every evaluator refusal from committed state (core/holdout.py gate_context) and appends the authorization record. The action (collect, count or read) runs only when that record is committed and pushed, because core.runner.context refuses an access log that differs from origin/main, and only under that record (gate.require_granted). It appends its completion record and run-log line even when it fails, and its results file has a fixed path under results/. A 'read' request before the final count and the last terminal-search window writes nothing, unless the read deadline has passed. Review round 10: refusals raised by core.runner.context before the evaluator runs (the study tree, the logs on origin/main, the runtime, the data files and the amendment lines) stop the command before any authorization record is written, because the committed state such a record would cite is not established; they are not logged as 'refused' records (F10). A 'count' and a 'read' each run in two committed steps (H2): the first run.py count or read fetches and seals the action's snapshot and appends a '<purpose>_fetch' run-log line with its sha256 and fetch-incomplete rate, and nothing else; the second, allowed only when that line is on origin/main, evaluates over that sealed snapshot alone, makes no request, and appends the results file, the run-log line and the completion. A discarded local second step therefore reproduces the same bytes, never a second draw of provider data. A retry reuses the sealed snapshot of the authorization it retries. Every holdout action refuses a local clock earlier than the commit time of origin/main's tip, and a read whose authorization record, or whose '_fetch' line, reached origin/main at or after the read deadline takes the not-read label (M2). Review round 11, F1 and F2: a refused 'read' authorization writes the not-read labels only under chronology.holdout.read_timing (4), never once a read has sealed its snapshot; due times come from the signed reach time of the authorization record, and a record timed after its commit reached origin/main is refused. Review round 14, F1: a count's or read's plan finds a per-event or quote request in an earlier sealed snapshot (a count's) only if that snapshot fetched it after the request's data end, the scheduled close of its 'end' session (daily bars, auctions) or its 'end' timestamp (minute bars, quotes); otherwise the request is fetched again into the action's own snapshot, which governs (core.holdout_store). The count at the close of the window's last session therefore never supplies the read with bars or prints that end before a delayed exit's session. Review round 14, F3: a count or read fetch step, and a stage fetch under its open start line, refuses when its snapshot directory already holds a sealed ledger that no committed line names (a discarded local attempt). Limitation: deleting that directory and the unpushed line defeats the check, as for the count-only run (exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path.runs); a second draw then differs only in which requests are fetch-incomplete, and every attempt runs under a committed authorization or start line. Review round 14, Codex P2: a results file that no committed line cites (a hard kill between the results rename and its line) never governs and does not refuse a retry: the next run under the same authorization recomputes from the same sealed snapshot, replaces that file, and its line and completion record the replaced sha256 (replaced_uncited_results_sha256). Once a committed line cites a count's or the read's results file, it is final.
access_log.rows_read: Review round 10, F13: a count's or read's completion reports rows_read, the normalized records held by the sealed snapshots it evaluated (its own and the collection batches it merged); a collect or amend completion reports 0.

study_code.rule: The frozen protocol records study_code = {tree: the git tree hash of blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/study/, fetch_tree: the git tree hash of blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/study/fetch/}. It pins trees only, never a commit: the repository squash-merges, so a PR-branch commit becomes unreachable, and every run appends run-log, access-log and amendment lines outside the tree, which moves HEAD (review round 7, C5). The study tree is merged to main before the freeze pull request, which does not change it. Every run checks out a commit reachable from origin/main whose blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/study tree equals the pinned tree (or a passing transport deviation of it), executes that tree, and reads the logs and data files of that same commit; the commit is recorded as provenance only. The tree holds the study code, the count-only code, the request plan and records (core/), the fetch transport (study/fetch/: HTTP client, authentication, pagination and retry only; review round 8, R8-1), the pinned copies (pinned_copies), the synthetic tests and study/runtime.lock. runtime.lock pins the Python version and numpy, pandas, exchange_calendars 4.13.2 and duckdb (review round 8, E1), with their dependencies. Every fetch and evaluation entry point refuses to run unless the protocol file at its fixed path has status frozen and study_code.tree equals the running tree, and unless study_code.parameters equals the code's parameters (review round 8, R8-4 and R8-2; core/guards.py, core/runner.py). The tree holds no data file (data_files). Every run, fetch and evaluator call names the tree and runtime it ran from. Development, validation and every holdout 'count' and 'read' run from this one tree, and the evaluator refuses any other (holdout_gate.evaluator_refusals). The only tree changes that keep a stage are transport deviations (transport_deviations). Review round 9: every entry point is run.py, run as python -I -B (runtime.lock run_command), which sets sys.pycache_prefix to a fresh directory before any study module is imported, so no bytecode cache in the tree is read; the tree may hold no other ignored file (F9). core.runner.context also refuses unless HEAD is reachable from origin/main and the run log, access log, deviations file and amendment files equal their origin/main content (F2; they are no longer ignored by .gitignore), and it reads the protocol from the freeze commit's blob, refusing a working copy or HEAD that differs from it (F3). A library call that bypasses run.py writes no run-log line, so its result can never govern (F8). Review round 10: core.runner.context (and the pre-freeze count-only and dry-run path, L1) also refuses unless the local origin/main equals the remote's main by git ls-remote (H2) and every version of the run log, access log, deviations file and amendment files on origin/main's first-parent history is a prefix of the next (M1). Every time the evaluator uses (the freeze time, and the reach times of amendment lines, access-log records, '_fetch' lines and the validation results) is the committer time of a commit whose signature verifies against GitHub's web-flow key, pinned as study/pinned/github-web-flow.gpg with fingerprint 968479A1AFF927E37D1A566BB5690EEEBB952194 (core.guards.verified_merge; M3), so a backdated client commit gives no time. The fetch transport runs in a child process (core/transport_proc.py), so no process that plans, parses or evaluates imports study/fetch/ (H1). runtime.lock pins every package's version and the sha256 of each installed dist-info RECORD, and the evaluator refuses any difference (L3). New entry points: run.py dry-run, transport-check and amend.

run_discipline.data_files: Data the study reads but may need to append to after the freeze live outside the study tree, in blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/data/: session-calendar.json and fees-v3.json (the base files, pinned by sha256 in the frozen protocol), and session-calendar-amendments.jsonl and fees-v3-amendments.jsonl (append-only, possibly empty at the freeze; each line in run_discipline.amendment_format). Appending a line never changes the study tree. The run log records each amendment file's sha256 and byte length at every run, and the evaluator refuses a file whose earlier logged content is not a byte prefix of its current content.

amendment_format.encoding: UTF-8 JSON Lines: one JSON object per line, each line ending in a newline; the files are append-only (run_discipline.data_files), so a line is never edited, reordered or removed

common_fields.schema_version: the integer 1 (this format); a line with another version is refused
common_fields.source: the primary source: an object with document (a non-empty string naming it), url (https on an official host of the line's kind), retrieved_at (an ISO date) and quotes (a non-empty list of non-empty verbatim passages that state the line's content)
common_fields.reason: a non-empty string saying why the line is appended

fields.session: the ISO date of a session of the pinned calendar (data/session-calendar.json) that the exchange will not open; removing a date that is not a pinned session is refused

fields.from: ISO date, inclusive, a charge (settlement) date (cost_model.fee_charge_dates)
fields.to: ISO date, inclusive, or null for an open-ended rate
fields.usd_per_million: a finite number >= 0: US dollars per million dollars of covered sales, as data/fees-v3.json sec_section31.rows

fields.from: ISO date, inclusive, a trade date (cost_model.fee_charge_dates)
fields.to: ISO date, inclusive, or null for an open-ended rate
fields.usd_per_share: a finite number >= 0: US dollars per share sold
fields.max_usd_per_trade: a finite number >= 0: the per-trade cap, as data/fees-v3.json finra_taf_covered_equity.rows

rules: Every listed field is required and no other field is allowed.
Dates are inclusive; to null means open-ended; from <= to when to is a date.
A calendar line's session and a fee line's from are on or after the freeze session; a line before it, or a line applied without a known freeze session, is refused.

Precedence: a fee line supersedes, for the dates it covers, every earlier row of its kind, the base file's rows (their open-ended last row included) and every earlier line: the latest appended line that covers a date governs, and a base row governs a date no line covers. No line is edited; supersession is by precedence.
A calendar line removes its session from the amended calendar; the freeze session and N0 keep the dates computed on the pinned, unamended calendar (chronology.holdout.window).

Every line is logged in the access log under purpose 'amend' before its deadline: 09:30 ET of the session it removes, or the first holdout count or read that uses a date it covers (populations.session_calendar, cost_model.fees).

run_discipline.run_log: blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/run-log.jsonl, append-only JSON lines. Every run of the frozen automation gets one line: each stage's fetch and re-fetch, development, validation, and each holdout 'count' and 'read', including failed and partial runs. Each line records the utc start and end, stage, purpose, commit run at (provenance) and study tree, runtime lock sha256, protocol_sha256 (review round 8, R8-2; every results file carries it too), data-file sha256s and amendment-file sha256s and byte lengths, input snapshot sha256s, status (complete, failed or partial) and the sha256 of the results file, if one was written (at most one per run, written atomically; run_discipline.once). For the validation results commit, it also records the GitHub-recorded time it became reachable from origin/main. Each line is committed and pushed before the next run of any stage starts. In code (review round 10, F13 and L3): the validation results commit's reach time is recorded as validation_results_reach_utc on every holdout 'count' and 'read' line (taken from the signed merge commit that first holds the file), and every line records runtime_environment_sha256, the sha256 of the installed distributions' RECORD digests and of every .pth file in the interpreter's site directories.
run_discipline.once: Development is computed by one logged run and validation by one logged run. A run holds every outcome in memory and writes the stage's results as one results file, atomically (temporary file, fsync, rename), only after every item of the stage is computed; no outcome is written before (review round 7, C1). A run that ends before that write has written no outcome and is not governing. It is logged as failed, and the stage may run again from the unchanged frozen tree on the same sealed inputs, each attempt logged; a retry cannot differ from an uninterrupted run, because the computation is deterministic (seeded streams, pinned runtime, sealed inputs). The first run of a stage that writes its results file is the stage's governing run. The governing development run's results are descriptive (multiple_testing.development_screen), and the governing validation run's results file governs the holdout gate. Each holdout 'count' and 'read' writes its results the same way, and each may be retried after a failed run with no results file under chronology.holdout.read_timing (review round 8, R8-6). In code (review round 9, F1, M-4 and F10): each development or validation stage is fetched by one logged run (a second fetch is refused unless every earlier attempt failed and sealed nothing) and evaluated into results/<stage>.json, a fixed path. An evaluation is refused when the stage already has a results line or file, when its snapshot is not the one its fetch line sealed, or when an earlier failed attempt used another snapshot. A run interrupted after its results file was written logs that file's sha256 as complete. Review round 11, F4: a stage fetch first appends a 'fetch_start' line and fetches only once that line is on origin/main (exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path.runs). Review round 11, F3: development is evaluated only after validation's complete fetch line is on origin/main, so no development outcome exists before the validation snapshot is sealed. Review round 13, F1: an evaluation runs in two committed steps, like a fetch: run.py evaluate first appends an 'evaluate_start' line naming the snapshot and computes nothing; the evaluation runs only once that line is on origin/main, and its end line cites it (start_index). Every attempt that could have computed an outcome is therefore a logged exposure with a signed time, which bounds when a void can apply (exposure_registry.update_rule); a failed attempt needs a new start line. Review round 14, Codex P2: recovery from a hard termination (SIGKILL, power loss) that no 'finally' block sees: a results file that no run-log line cites never governs and no longer refuses the retry. The next evaluation under the open start line recomputes from the same sealed snapshot, replaces that file (atomic_write_results replaces only the file whose sha256 the caller names), and its line records the replaced sha256 as replaced_uncited_results_sha256; the same holds for a holdout count and read. A file that a line cites refuses a second evaluation as before.
run_discipline.deviations: Any change to the study tree after the freeze is a numbered deviation in blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/deviations.json (cause, diff reference, new tree hash, affected stages), committed and pushed before any run from the new tree. A run from a deviated tree is refused by core.guards.check_study_tree (review round 11, C14: the code is stricter than the earlier 'reported beside' wording, which described an output that cannot exist), so it never governs a stage, the holdout gate or the extension decision. There is no exception for a rerun after a code change, whatever the cause and whatever it reproduces (review round 7, C1 and C2): a stage that cannot complete from the unchanged frozen tree is void. A void development stage reports every item as underpowered there (development gates nothing). A void validation stage voids the holdout of this protocol version (every item scores p = 1 at validation). A void holdout 'count' or 'read' labels every carried item 'not supported (holdout not read)' with the reason (chronology.holdout.read_timing). Transport deviations (transport_deviations) are the only tree changes that keep a stage, and they change no evaluation code.
run_discipline.fetch: Before any outcome of a stage (development, validation, and each holdout 'count' or 'read'), the frozen code fetches every quote window, minute bar, per-event daily bar and official print that stage needs, and for development and validation first the full 2016-2020 screen data (universe_and_identity.request_shapes), under universe_and_identity.asof. Review round 8, R8-1: the request plan (symbols, asof, sessions, stamps, entry, exit, search and backward windows, and the enumeration) is derived by core/plan.py and core/stage.py, in the evaluation tree, only from sealed inputs (the calendar, the enumeration, corporate-action records, decision-time inputs, and the timestamps and eligibility of already sealed quotes); the loop core/driver.py fetches every planned request not yet sealed until the plan adds nothing. study/fetch/ receives one planned request and returns its raw pages; it derives nothing and parses no row. Terminal-search windows of censored trades extend past the segment end (populations.terminal_exits.segment_end), and backward windows follow populations.terminal_exits.booking (R8-7). The result is sealed as a sha256-pinned private snapshot (the ledger's sha256; the ledger holds every page's sha256 and normalized-record sha256), and that sha256 and the stage's fetch-incomplete rate by kind are committed in the run log. At most one re-fetch is allowed: once, of only the fetch-incomplete requests, before any outcome of that stage, followed by fetching any window that only then became plannable, committed the same way. After it, the 1% void rule is final. No outcome is computed from unsealed data.
run_discipline.synthetic_tests: The evaluator refuses a results file whose run-log entry names a tree other than the pinned one, a holdout count or read from a tree other than the pinned one or a passing transport deviation of it, a transport deviation without a passing reproduction check, a runtime that differs from runtime.lock, an edited (not appended) amendment file, a second results file for a stage, a read retry that chronology.holdout.read_timing does not permit, and an outcome computed before the stage's fetch rate is committed. It accepts a run from a commit reachable from origin/main whose study tree equals the pinned tree, with run-log, access-log and amendment lines committed after the freeze. A test kills a run before its results write and asserts that nothing was written and that the retry reproduces an uninterrupted run byte for byte. The suite is study/tests/, run by study_code.test_command under study/runtime.lock. Review round 9 (F6) adds command-level tests against a temporary repository shaped like this one after the freeze (tests/fixture_repo.py), so no test depends on the real protocol's status or writes to the real run log: every command refusing on a draft, a stage fetched once and evaluated into one results file with a kill after the write, the context refusals (bytecode isolation and ignored files, logs off origin/main, a protocol edited after the freeze, amendment timing, coverage_decision, transport deviations), the count-only command, and the holdout path through collect, count with two extensions and read, with two batches of different enumerations and a rename re-fetch, and the not-read label after the deadline.
run_discipline.pinned_copies: The study tree imports no module outside itself except the Python standard library, numpy, pandas, exchange_calendars and duckdb (review round 7, F6; review round 8, E1 adds duckdb, which the pinned dedupe_identity needs). It holds byte-for-byte copies of the external definitions it needs, listed in study/pinned_copies.json as (source path, commit aa6fc79, git blob, sha256, definition names): the Bars class and ET, et_epoch, TIME_BUCKETS, PRICE_TIERS, DV_TIERS, time_bucket, price_tier and dv_tier from mover-early-entry rules.py (R8-12); official_price from sessions_io.py; valid_quote from quotes.py; dedupe_identity with DUPLICATE_SERIES_MIN_SESSIONS, DUPLICATE_SERIES_MIN_SPAN_COVERAGE, CONTINUITY_RATIO, _rename_terminus and _components from broad-universe coverage.py; DATA_SYMBOL from collect_daily.py. A synthetic test reads each source with git cat-file at the listed blob, checks the blob hash and sha256, extracts each named definition with ast (decorators included) and asserts that the copy is identical and holds nothing else. Because nothing outside the tree is imported, a later edit to those paths on main cannot reach a run, and no module-level code of rules.py, quotes.py or coverage.py (their fees.json, protocol.json and duckdb-connection code) ever runs.
run_discipline.transport_deviations: The fetch transport must work against a live API for 12-18 months (review round 7, C2). Review round 8, R8-1: study/fetch/ holds only the transport (HTTP client, host, endpoint path, authentication header, pagination and retry); the request plan, the stamps and windows, the enumeration, response parsing and row filtering are evaluation code outside it, so no change under study/fetch/ can change a request, a stamp, a window, the parsing or the evaluation. It can change which bytes arrive (review round 11, F3: the child process returns raw pages that the parent parses), which the reproduction check below bounds by sampling and does not exclude. A deviation that changes only files under study/fetch/ is a transport deviation. Before any run from the new tree, it passes a committed reproduction check against the most recently sealed snapshot of each request kind that exists (or the snapshot of the pre-freeze native dry run, freeze_preconditions): (a) the new tree regenerates the request plan from the sealed inputs and its canonical request records equal the sealed request records byte for byte; (b) every sealed raw page, re-parsed offline, gives byte-identical normalized records (its sealed normalized_sha256), for every page, not a sample; (c) the new transport re-requests the first 200 requests of each kind, in sha256 order of their request records, and their merged normalized records equal the sealed ones (core/transport_check.py). The result is committed in deviations.json with the deviation. A passing transport deviation may govern every later fetch, collection batch, count and read, whose results carry the qualifier 'transport-deviation'. A deviation that touches any file outside study/fetch/, or fails the check, is an ordinary deviation (deviations). Limitation: a change of the provider's response format needs a parser change outside study/fetch/, which is an ordinary deviation. If no passing transport deviation restores collection or fetching in time, the affected sessions are late-collected (holdout_gate.prospective_collection) or the read misses its deadline, and chronology.holdout.read_timing applies. Record format (review round 9, H-2): deviations.json is {"deviations": [...]}, and a transport deviation carries number, kind 'transport', cause, diff_reference, new_tree, new_fetch_tree, affected_stages and transport_check (the reproduction check's result, with passes). core.guards.check_study_tree accepts a running tree other than the pinned one only when a committed entry names it as new_tree and the running study/fetch/ tree as new_fetch_tree, its transport_check passed, and the pinned tree and it differ only in paths under fetch/. Every result from it carries 'transport-deviation'. Review round 10, H1 and F6: the reproduction check runs only as run.py transport-check from the new tree (which may differ from the pinned tree only under fetch/), against a development or validation snapshot sealed by that stage's logged fetch (it holds every screen and per-event request kind). It writes results/transport-check-<first 12 characters of the new tree>.json with a 'transport_check' run-log line. transport_check in the deviation must carry passes, output_path and output_sha256, and core.guards.check_study_tree accepts the deviation only when that committed output says passes for the new tree and a complete run-log line from the new tree wrote it; a self-declared passes: true is refused. Because the transport runs in a child process that returns raw bytes only, a change under fetch/ cannot alter planning, parsing, seeds, statistics or labels, and (a) and (b) need no rerun at run time: they are deterministic functions of unchanged code and sealed bytes, bound by the output's hash. Limitation: (c) keeps the fixed sample of the first 200 requests per kind in sha256 order of their request records. Any committed rule is known in advance, and an unpredictable sample could not be reproduced, so a transport written to alter only unsampled responses is not caught by (c). A stage snapshot holds no enumeration request (assets and corporate actions come from the count-only part 0 and the collection batches), so transport-check does not re-request those kinds, and a change that alters only them is not caught by (c). Review round 11, F3: (c) samples 200 requests per kind in sha256 order of the seed followed by the request record, where the seed is the id of the first origin/main commit holding the new tree, a signed merge made after the transport was written, so the sample cannot be known when the transport is written. transport-check also runs (b) and (c) against every sealed holdout snapshot (collection batches and count and read snapshots) and refuses without --holdout-root once one exists; (a) is not rerun for them, since it is a deterministic function of the unchanged plan code. Development is evaluated only after validation's fetch line is on origin/main, which closes the window between development results and the validation fetch. A holdout read under a passing transport deviation may support a claim, with the qualifier 'transport-deviation'. Limitation: a transport that alters responses of unsampled requests only is still not caught, now with a probability set by the unpredictable sample. Review round 15, N02 (R14-open-2): run.py transport-check seals each live sample (c) under <snapshot root>/transport-check-<tree>-live/<label> before it computes the check from the seals (core.transport_check.seal_live_samples and reproduction_from_sealed), and the output names each sample's sha256 (live_snapshots). A sample already sealed there by a killed run is read, never drawn again, and an output that a hard kill left with no run-log line is adopted only if it equals the check recomputed from the seals.
