The count excludes a trade as 'undefined_factor' when E traded (its raw bar exists) and the booking at E is undefined, which is exactly when a normal exit is excluded by the read; with no bar on E (a halt or a delisting) the count keeps the trade, since a terminal trade stays in the statistic. H3-c's count applies the spin-off record and every overnight leg's accounting. Residual (in $.chronology.holdout.count_unit): exit-window fetch failures, delayed-exit accounting and records after E, and H3-c's positivity check stay read-only; count_unit only decides extensions, and every minimum uses the read's n. The count path still calls no price or return function (test_count_path_calls_no_price_or_return_function passes with cash_term forbidden). Tests: tests/test_trades.py Round15Accounting test_the_count_excludes_what_the_read_excludes_for_an_undefined_factor and test_the_h3c_count_applies_the_reads_leg_accounting; on the code before this change the count returns 'counted' where the read returns 'undefined_factor'.

review_record.input: Review round 15, N06 (major): retained uncarried splits were checked only through the planned exit E, although a delayed exit holds the position through E+5, so a split during that extension could bypass the exclusion; the price-independent check should run through the actual exit, with a delayed-exit split test.
review_record.resolution: Resolved. For a trade that fills after E, core.trades.trade re-applies core.trades.record_exclusion over (entry session, actual exit session] before booking (a split record with F = 1 there, or a spin-off record, excludes it, with the exit session recorded). The count, which never sees the exit, keeps the check through E (its residual, $.chronology.holdout.count_unit). Protocol: $.populations.suspected_unadjusted_split. Test: tests/test_trades.py Round15Accounting test_a_split_record_during_a_delayed_exit_excludes_the_trade (no quote on E or E+1, a fill on E+2 and a forward split record effective that day with F = 1): now split_record_excluded; on the code before this change it was booked as a delayed exit at the post-split price.

review_record.input: Review round 15, F06 (undefined bootstrap cases; partially resolved, blocker remaining): the minima had no occupied-session requirement, and the confidence bounds discarded undefined draws (core/stats.py bound), so H1-D could meet its per-group minimum in one occupied entry session and, with coinciding group means, get a zero-width interval and 'not_supported_mde_excluded'. Occupied-cluster eligibility and invalid or degenerate-inference rules controlling both support and exclusion were asked for, with concentrated-session tests.
review_record.resolution: Resolved with the rules derived from the preregistered bootstrap and levels; one stricter option is left open (below). core/stats.py conservative_bound: the MDE-exclusion bounds use all B draws, an undefined draw placed beyond the defined ones on the side that cannot support an exclusion (equal to numpy's linear quantile when every draw is defined). inference_check: occupied-cluster eligibility (the undefined-draw share, draws in which the item or an H1-D group has no trade, at most the item's tail level, 0.01 one-sided, 0.005 for H3-c) and non-degenerate draws (at least two, not all equal); mde_excluded requires it, and item_label's inference_ok makes an invalid item 'underpowered', so it controls a pass and an exclusion alike. core/evaluate.py reports occupied_sessions (per group for H1-D), units and the inference record per item. Protocol: $.statistics.p_value, $.statistics.inference_validity (new), $.outcome_reporting.labels.not_supported_mde_excluded and .underpowered. Tests: tests/test_stats.py ConcentratedSessions: one occupied session with coinciding means (at e7529b47 labelled not_supported_mde_excluded on the interval [0, 0]; now underpowered, 36% undefined draws), sessions spread over 6+ blocks restore valid inference, degenerate draws support neither a pass nor an exclusion, and the conservative bounds. Open decision (not guessed): whether to preregister, in addition, a fixed floor of distinct occupied entry sessions per item or H1-D group for few-cluster bias (options: none beyond the bootstrap-implied ~5-6 spread sessions, as now; a floor such as 20 or 30 sessions from the cluster-robust few-cluster literature; or n_min / DEFF sessions from the preregistered minima and DEFF 1.5 under full within-session correlation, 100/67/67 per H1-D group and 200/100/100 per cell). Recommendation: keep the bootstrap-derived rule and add a floor of 20 occupied sessions per item or group at the next cross-family review, stated with its source, which would also need a count_unit key for the extension decision.

review_record.input: Review round 15, F14 (MDE units and occupied sessions; partially resolved): H3-c kept the misleading mde_percent_H3-c name, and the item outputs lacked occupied-session counts for the primary contrasts (core/evaluate.py).
review_record.resolution: Resolved. $.minimum_detectable_effect.mde_percent_H3-c is renamed mde_log_points_H3-c, and a new $.minimum_detectable_effect.units states that the tables are 100 x the MDE: percent of the return for H1-D and the cells, log points (100 x a difference of mean log returns) for H3-c. core/evaluate.py item_result reports units and occupied_sessions for every item, per group ({high, low}) for H1-D. Test: tests/test_stats.py ConcentratedSessions test_one_occupied_session_supports_no_exclusion asserts the per-group occupied sessions; on the code before this change the key does not exist.

review_record.input: Review round 15, F07 (hypothesis-level verdicts; unresolved, major): $.outcome_reporting.hypothesis_verdict and core/stats.py hypothesis_verdict promoted any associated passing item into an H1 or H3 verdict, and tests/test_stats.py accepted H3 screening from H3-a alone; the primary contrasts should get their own verdicts and profitability should be reported separately.
review_record.resolution: Resolved. core/stats.py hypothesis_verdict now reads only the primary contrast (H1-D for H1, H3-c for H3): its pass name gives the pass verdict with its qualifiers, not_supported_mde_excluded gives 'not supported', 'not supported (holdout not read)' passes through at the holdout, anything else (a contaminated pass included) is 'inconclusive', and a hypothesis whose contrast was not carried has no holdout verdict. core/stats.py profitability reports the tradable cells separately (hypothesis, label, pass, qualifiers); core/evaluate.py and the not-read record (core/holdout.py not_read_results) carry it. The holdout gate still opens for every validated item. Protocol: $.outcome_reporting.hypothesis_verdict (rewritten) and $.outcome_reporting.profitability (new). Tests: tests/test_stats.py Labels test_verdicts_come_from_the_primary_contrasts_and_cells_are_reported_apart and test_verdicts_at_the_holdout replace the tests that accepted a cell-driven verdict; tests/test_holdout.py's not-read case now expects no H3 verdict when H3-c is not carried. On the code before this change H1 is 'screened' on H1-D-b_lane-low alone and profitability does not exist.

review_record.input: Review round 15, F10 (H3-a embargo; unresolved, major): $.chronology.boundaries and core/trades.py exempted H3-a from the embargo although its exits can be delayed to E+5, and tests/test_trades.py asserted the exemption; purging should cover its permitted actual horizon, and its block-length rationale should be revisited.
review_record.resolution: Resolved. core/trades.py embargoes every arm (the multi-session exemption list is gone), so H3-a's entries in the first 6 sessions of validation and after a dropped year are 'embargoed' like the others; the 6-session embargo covers the E+5 search of the earlier segment's trades. Block length: H3-a's 5 sessions assumed a same-session hold, but its permitted horizon is 6 sessions (t+1 through E+5), longer than the block; $.run_discipline.study_code.parameters.bootstrap.block_sessions.H3-a (core/params.py) is now 10, the length every other item uses, which covers the longest permitted hold (b_lane's 5 sessions and its E+5 search); a per-item 6 was not adopted, to keep one rule rather than tuning per item. Protocol: $.chronology.boundaries, $.statistics.bootstrap, $.run_discipline.study_code.parameters. Tests: tests/test_trades.py test_embargo_applies_to_every_arm (replacing the test that asserted the exemption) and tests/test_e2e.py (an early-January H3-a entry is now embargoed: 6 filled H3-a trades, not 7). On the code before this change the H3-a entry is not embargoed and the block length is 5.

overturn: Any headline result is overturned if a rerun on the same frozen inputs, study tree and runtime.lock does not reproduce it byte for byte, if an independent quote sample puts the cost table off by more than 2x, or if the access log shows a holdout read that no committed granted entry preceded.

study_code_status.summary: Code-first preregistration of the core: the study tree at run_discipline.study_code.path implements the rules of this draft, and its synthetic suite passes under study/runtime.lock (run_discipline.study_code.test_record). Review round 9 wired every entry point through run.py: the pre-freeze count-only run (count-only), each development and validation stage fetched and evaluated once (fetch, evaluate), and the holdout path (authorize, collect, count, read), each refusing unless its logs are on origin/main and the protocol is the freeze commit's blob. No market data was read, no provider was called and no outcome was computed; every test input is synthetic, and the command-level tests run against a temporary repository. Review round 10 bound transport deviations to a logged reproduction check and moved the transport into a child process, split each holdout count and read into a sealed fetch step and an evaluation step, took every freeze and reach time from commits signed by GitHub's pinned web-flow key, checked origin/main against the remote and the logs' append-only history, and added the dry-run, transport-check and amend commands. Review round 11 bounded the dry run by every request's reach, made the holdout read independent of its outcome (a sealed read is always evaluated and a refused authorization cannot be held back), paced the transport at the pinned rate limit, judged late collection per session and every holdout due time by signed reach times, added pushed start lines before every pre-freeze and stage fetch, and extended the transport check to holdout snapshots with a seeded sample. Review round 12 took two independent reviews, one cross-family (Codex) and one Claude: identity dedup is decided as of each candidate session, holdout evaluations read only the base snapshots their seal pinned, quotes are ordered by exact nanosecond stamps, diagnostic splits cluster by session, a sealed read can be retried after the deadline, and the freeze needs a passing identity probe and fetch margin at the pinned rate. Review round 13 took a second pair of reviews (Claude and cross-family Codex): void deviations apply only before the outcome they would void could be computed (the validation evaluation's pushed start line, or the holdout gate's opening) and are reported, never applied, after it; evaluations run under pushed start lines; identity survivors are chosen from rename records effective by t with no current active status; a failed count is retried only as a retry; retried counts read their first attempt's snapshot directory; identical quote updates inside a page are kept in provider order; and fee first use covers a read's terminal-search sessions. Review round 14 took a third pair of reviews (Claude and cross-family Codex): the validation file is bound by sha256 from the authorization to every count and read; a read refetches per-event bars, prints and quotes that an earlier count fetched before their data end; fee amendments supersede by precedence and a fee gap is refused before any count or read fetch; the dividend cash is taken per ex-date at the previous close; a results file left by a hard kill is recomputed on the retry; and two items that need a redesign are listed in open_before_first_holdout_count, which must be empty before the first holdout count.
